This low-stress, forage-rich environment allows our birds to express natural behaviors while building healthier soil through regenerative practices. The result? name: Uphill Farmers
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Eggs; Eggs (Chicken); Eggs (Other); Meat & Poultry; Livestock for Sale; Rabbit
notes: Uphill Farmers is a humble two-person operation located in Marrowstone Island, Washington, on the Olympic Peninsula. Ren specializes in heritage turkeys and meat and fur rabbits, while Dimitri’s focus is on specialty geese and chickens. Together, the two of us have merged our passion for local agriculture, humane livestock husbandry, and accessible local foods to create Uphill Farmers. We pride ourselves on producing animals that are healthy, happy, high-quality, and with friendly temperaments. Our primary specialty is producing high-welfare livestock for sale for other farmers, breeders, and homesteaders. To quote The Livestock Conservancy, “Rare farm animals represent an irreplaceable piece of earth’s biodiversity and offer incredible variety that may be needed for future farms – robust health, mothering instincts, foraging, and the ability to thrive in a changing climate. These farm animals are a vital part of ensuring food security for our planet – now and for the future.” Many of our modern-day farm animals have been bred – sometimes to extremes – to produce the most food at the lowest upfront cost. This often sacrifices welfare, disease resistance, overall health, climate tolerance, and other desirable traits, as well as turning farm animal species into genetic monocultures. The future for these production-breed animals is not a sustainable one; they are not resilient in the face of epidemics, changing climate, and evolving farm methods.

Over the years, we have transitioned from a send-to-the-warehouse pack-and-ship orchard into a sell-direct-to-the-public marketed U-pick and farm-stand. Starting in June, we have three varieties of cherries: Coral Champagne, Bing, and Rainier. Then, as the summer progresses, we have peaches and nectarines. Toward the end of the season, which ends in September, we have Seedless table grapes, pluots, and apples. We communicate through our website, thestutzmanranch.com, by posting what is available and when. The U-pick season is unpredictable with weather and ripening schedules. Plus, we never know how many people will come to pick at our 15-acre orchard or how much they will pick. During the season our website stating availability and what is ripe can change on a daily basis.

notes: Metta Farm is a small-scale farm located in Woodinville, WA, specializing in the cultivation of Asian heritage vegetables and herbs. Metta is a Pali (ancient Indian) word that means loving-kindness, which is the farm’s core value, and the way every living being is treated on the farm. Metta Farm stands behind its name and core value in aiming to keep the land and the community healthy, and to provide fresh and nutrient-dense produce to the community through using no-till, regenerative, and organic farming practices that promote biodiversity, increase soil health, and attract natural predators to attend to garden pests. These practices include using only non-GMO seeds, organic compost and inputs, and preventive pest management (physical barrier, crop rotation, companion planting, good sanitation, etc.). Metta Farm is a solo woman farm owned and operated by Sherry Yuan. Sherry left her previous career in the corporate world to pursue farming due to her love of nature and a desire to serve and provide for the community. As the farm matures and evolves, Sherry hopes to provide not just fresh produce to the local community but also promote healthy living through grower and food education, and provide a relaxing space for the community members to socialize, destress, and escape the angst of everyday life.

name: Westcott Bay Shellfish Company
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Seafood; Clams; Mussels; Oysters
notes: In the late 70’s, the Westcott Bay tidelands were home to a thriving shellfish operation called Westcott Bay Seafarms, which raised renowned oysters that appeared on menus across the country. Over the years the farm went into steady decline, and was put up for sale as a home site. Henry Island residents Erik and Andrea Anderson bought the dilapidated property in 2013 with the vision of restoring it to its former glory and honoring its legacy in the San Juan Islands community. Over the years, Erik and Andrea have worked to replant the depleted shellfish crops, rebuild and replace farm infrastructure, and compile a group of dedicated people to create our Westcott Family. Today, Westcott Bay Shellfish Co. is one of the few small, family-run aquaculture farms in the San Juan Islands. The soul of Westcott Bay is a philosophy of community and environmental stewardship, and a respect for its unique natural and cultural history. We invite you to come and enjoy our laid-back, friendly atmosphere and experience life on a working aquaculture farm. We have a lot going on at our little farm! We grow clams, mussels, and oysters. We harvest our shellfish daily, and sell it at our Farm Store where our farm crew hand selects the shellfish for you. In the summer season we open up our Tide Tables picnic area where you can enjoy our BBQ’d oysters and an assortment of fresh, locally sourced dishes to accompany your shellfish. Did we mention the tables are right on the water? It’s lunch, and a show. You can watch the wildlife, the tides come in and out, and usually our farm crew hard at work. We slow down a bit in the winter months, so we have opened up our beautiful Net Shed Kitchen. It is an intimate and cozy space with a commercial kitchen that allows us to make fun seasonal dishes all winter long.

name: Fog & Fleece Sheepery
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Meat & Poultry; Livestock for Sale; Locally Made; Yarn, Fiber & Wool
notes: Fog & Fleece Sheepery is a small but diverse sheep farm with a focus on fiber and education. After interning under a local shepherd for three years, we took over the property with our own vision of offering a space for community gathering and learning. At this time we raise Icelandic, Shetland, and Romney sheep and market mostly to the fiber community, but we do focus on whole animal use and dual (and triple!) purpose breeds and management. We host workshops, classes, and lectures, as well as on-farm community events like movie nights, lamb yoga, and something we call the Maker’s Meadow, which is an open pasture event for fiber artists. We also offer a space for teachers to teach at little or no cost, and for people to build community. The farm is open for events with a farm store on property that’s open during the summer months. Our property is an family owned farm that’s been passed down through three generations, with a heritage barn built in 1932. Originally a dairy, started by German immigrants, the property has hosted fiber animals, hay production, and now sheep!

They will be barking at you but their tails will be wagging which means that you have to pet them as they are very happy to see you. We will introduce them to you along with their history and purpose on the farm. We will then take you into the barn, let the dogs into the barn so you can interact with them some more. They love our visitors! You will then learn about the history of llamas and alpacas. We have two large bags of fiber, one llama and one alpaca, so you can run your fingers through them to see the differences. Then we proceed through the barn out to the area where the female alpacas and llamas are waiting for you. Some of them love to be petted and interact with you. There is a very large roofed overhang over this area so you won’t get wet if it is raining. The animals like being out of the rain too! After mingling with the animals, we proceed back through the barn to our farm store which is stocked with roving and yarn from our animals, camels, and other alpacas and llamas as well as blankets, clothing, hats, gloves, mittens, socks, and stuffed alpaca and llama dolls and bears as well as other great items. We also have fresh eggs for sale from our 21 chickens. This entire experience can take as much as two hours. So, plan accordingly. SEE YA AT THE FARM SOON!

products_text: Chestnuts; Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Eggs; Eggs (Chicken); Eggs (Duck); Fruit & Berries; Apples; Currants; Raspberries; Meat & Poultry; Bacon; Beef; Ground Meat; Ham; Lamb; Pork; Nuts; Locally Made; Home & Personal Care
notes: We are Regeneration Acres, selling Eggs, Pastured Poultry, Pork, Beef, Lamb, Seasonal Fruits, and Handmade Soaps. Our farm is located in the heart of Onalaska, which is located in Southwest Washington, about 10 miles off of I-5 and almost equidistant from Seattle, WA and Portland, OR. It is a small community of about 800 people with a thriving community of local business and a high percentage of productive farms. Our farm is just below the foothills of the cascades. On a clear day we have a direct view of Mt. Saint Helens just south of us. Around us you can get a view of Mt. Rainer, and even Mt. Adams. We label our handmade soap as Three Peaks in honor of these three beautiful volcanoes. As you go east of our farm you will head towards some of the most sought-after recreational areas of Lewis County, including Mayfield Lake, the Cowlitz and Cispus Rivers, and Riffe Lake. When you stop by our farm we encourage you to explore the area. You will not be disappointed. Regeneration Acres was founded out of a passion for sustainability and a desire to make a positive impact on the environment. The journey began with a simple question: How can agriculture restore and enrich the land, rather than deplete it? Inspired by the principles of regenerative farming, the founders set out to create a farm that would serve as a model for responsible stewardship. From the very beginning, Regeneration Acres adopted practices that prioritize soil health, biodiversity, and ecological balance. Cover crops, rotational grazing, and agroforestry principles became the foundation of the farm’s approach. Every decision was guided by a commitment to sustainability—ensuring that the land would remain productive and vibrant for generations to come. The motto, “Regenerating Nature, Cultivating Tomorrow” reflects the farm’s dedication to building a better future through sustainable practices. Today, Regeneration Acres stands as a testament to what’s possible when innovation, care for natural resources, and a vision for the future come together. It’s more than a farm—it’s a living example of regeneration in action. Mission Statement: To restore the land and grow nourishing food through sustainable, regenerative farming—building a healthier future for our community and the environment.

products_text: Chestnuts; Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Eggs; Eggs (Chicken); Eggs (Other); Flowers, Nursery & Trees; Bamboo; Lavender; Fruit & Berries; Apples; Aronia Berries; Berries; Blueberries; Cherries; Currants; Figs; Grapes; Kiwi Berries; Pears; Pears (Asian); Plums/Prunes/Pluots; Raspberries; Tayberries; Meat & Poultry; Beef; Chicken; Lamb; Livestock for Sale; Poultry; Hazelnuts; Nuts; Walnuts; Vegetables & Herbs; Artichokes; Asparagus; Eggplant; Fennel; Green Onions; Herbs (Fresh); Lemongrass; Lettuce; Oregano; Parsley; Pumpkins; Rhubarb; Thyme; Tomatoes (Cherry)
notes: We’ve designed systems so that the farm takes care of itself and makes less work for the farmer: 1) I get livestock to eat weeds and do pest control with rotational paddock grazing. 2) I save on water and deny weeds with drip irrigation and lots of woodchip mulch. 3) I kill rabbits and wild geese that steal produce with dogs that are trained to hunt in a pack. 4) Dogs also herd livestock without drawing blood so I don’t have to chase livestock. 5) sheep and pigs feed the dogs with their meat and bones. 6) The pigs and chickens excrete in a designated woodchip area that the pigs constantly mix for me along with all kitchen scraps and produce overflow creating a rich mulch that I put on garden beds once a year when I swap it for fresh wood chips. 7) In the fall our pigs walk with us through the orchards and eat windfall apples and pears. They can barely walk when we return them to the barn because the phrase “eats like a pig” is completely true. We always butcher pigs after the last apple has fallen! With only 20 acres we have 9 separate areas that are either livestock paddocks or crops that the livestock must be kept away from. So 9 microfarms–basically a Japanese size. I even have studied Japanese style mini farms that are maximally efficient and, of course, the highest quality product so as to get niche market high prices. Japan leads the world in microfarm techniques. The first time I flew to Japan in 1992, I freaked out seeing all the tiny farms along the train tracks that basically looked like the size of backyards in American suburbs but had small tractors doing real farming. I thought they couldn’t possibly be big enough to make a profit! My wife and I also have a wedding venue here at Taber Ranch. It’s a working farm with a beautiful event field right at its center.

notes: Since 2000, we have been providing our community with healthy meat from our Wagyu beef cows, Icelandic sheep and heritage breeds of pigs. Although not certified Organic, we use organic practices. Our cows and sheep are 100% grass fed. They graze our irrigated fields in the summer in a rotational patter. They always have shelter from the sun and in the winter spend their time in an open barn with a small pasture and are fed our own hay. Our pigs spend the summer in the woods and the winter in a large open barn. They are fed organic grain, yogurt made from our own dairy cows and fruits and vegetables gleaned from neighboring vegetable farms and our own supplies. Happy healthy animals are easy to take care of. It is our job as farmers to provide the best environment we can for our animals. If you were a cow, sheep or a pig, you would want to live on our farm. We have an email list of people that are interested in getting products from us. We send out quarterly newsletters with links to our order forms. We sell beef and pork by the whole, 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8. Our lamb is sold by the whole or the half. If you are interested in being on our email list and to have access to this very high quality meat, send an email to Selma@bonedryridgefarm.com

notes: We are Mitch and Michelle Lewis; first-generation, late-in-life farmers and hosts, co-owners and stewards of Summit Farms, our 28 environmentally-protected acres. The land was homesteaded in 1907, and includes a renovated – though rustic – WA heritage barn, three green-houses/high-tunnels, a root-cellar, plus amenities including a cedar-lined Finnish sauna, swingset and play-areas. We grow vegetables and herbs from seed to sale through the Olympia Farmers Market, Tumwater Farmers Market, South Sound Fresh and occasionally on-site. We specialize in most ingredients for salsas, salads, or pickling including hot peppers, boutique tomatoes, onion and garlic varieties plus cucumbers, squash, lettuce, carrots and other seasonal herbs. We are zoned AgriTourism (and head the county advisory board), and offer (through HipCamp) 3-4 RV spaces with full hook-ups, along with 4-5 “dry-camp” sites that are well separated. We also offer experiences in the upper barn including karaoke, family movie night, billiards, swings and a stage with pro audio/video equipment and band instruments (drums, keyboard, guitar, mic, mixer e.g.). We love to host small (10+) to large (100-150) groups for reunions, board meetings, off-sites, corporate events and (occasionally) weddings/renewal of vows. We believe and practice natural and regenerative growing methods and work with groups and agencies such as USDA/NRCS, Thurston Conservation District, Partners US Fish & Wildlife, WSU, Experience Olympia & Beyond to conserve and better our land for our grandchildren’s grandchildren. Very welcome to Summit Farms!

name: Hearth & Hollow
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Edible Flowers; Seeds & Starts; Plants/Plant Starts; Seeds; Vegetable/Herb starts; Vegetables & Herbs; Locally Made; Preserved & Pantry Items; Jams & Spreads
notes: Hearth & Hollow is a micro-nursery and plant CSA located in Vancouver, WA. Hearth & Hollow helps local families grow their own food with seasonal plant starts, CSA shares, and simple guidance. We make gardening accessible, whether you’re planting your first lettuce or filling raised beds for the season. Why Hearth & Hollow Big box stores sell generic, often unhealthy plants grown with unidentified synthetic fertilizers. Our starts are grown in organic soil, from seed, right here in the Pacific Northwest. When you buy from us, you’re not just getting plants. You’re supporting regenerative agricultural practices, keeping your dollars local, and ensuring you’re feeding your family clean, fresh food. Our Story Hi, I’m Dusti. I’m a marketer by trade, but business has never been just about income for me – it’s about people, participation, and presence. When the 2025 inauguration happened, a voice in my head kept saying: plant something. Before I knew what I was doing, I was starting seeds in trays, building a greenhouse in my suburban backyard, and signing up for my first market. But the truth is, growing food is in my blood. I grew up in Oregon summers snapping beans at a crowded kitchen table, trailing my great-grandpa down rows of raspberries and green beans while jars clinked in the canning line. My great-grandparents were Depression-era gardeners who treated a backyard like a small farm and taught us to plant, harvest, and put food by. Now I’m combining that heritage with years of building businesses and teaching online to make gardening simple, approachable, and doable. Our Ethos At Hearth & Hollow, we are committed to increasing food sovereignty and reducing waste. Here’s how we do that: – We source donated pots, repurpose trays and supplies, and lean on neighbor networks to reduce our consumption. – We maintain a directory dedicated to helping people in Clark County find and access food. – We participate in organizations and initiatives where we can share tools, knowledge, and guidance alongside the plants themselves. Our Products We specialize in edible plant starts and local small-batch preserves, including our famous candied jalapeños.

name: Farm and Food Justice Network
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Eggs; Eggs (Chicken); Fruit & Berries; Grains & Pulses; Seeds & Starts; Vegetables & Herbs; Locally Made; Local Food Box; Preserved & Pantry Items
notes: Farm and Food Justice Network farmers collaborate to aggregate, market, and distribute food and wisdom. Our mission is to enhance the capacity of farms and food enterprises to be climate resilient. We prioritize farmers supporting farmers networking to gain equitable access to resources and support. Our vision is for locally-grown food in our region to reach vulnerable families in our communities. The Food and Farm Justice Network (FFJN) offers a community-wide plan to improve local food access and reduce vehicle miles traveled. Among the wrap-around food justice initiatives, FFJN works to ensure producers access to grants, technical assistance, and training, so that workers and farmers can improve economic conditions, share skills, and supply food while reducing miles traveled. Contact us to join our Google group via https://farmfoodjustice.net/. By cooperating, farmers are working to improve aggregation and distribution capacity required to overcome the undue burdens of economic hardship, climate change, and unmitigated environmentally dangerous working conditions. We uplift social and environmental justice, farm and food business viability, nutritional diversity, and food sovereignty. We are growing food in our community for our community and supporting economic prosperity.

notes: We strive to bring you ethically and naturally raised meats from our farm to your freezer. With a strong focus on regenerative land stewarding and organic practices, we are dedicated to providing all our livestock with no bad days. Our pigs, chickens, turkeys & quail are pasture raised on no-spray land. Rotational grazing methods help us to achieve full, lush pastures for our animals to graze. By partnering with nature, our land is able to give back year after year. Though we are not a closed loop farm, many of our animals come from trusted, local farms whose values align with ours. We hatch a large number of our poultry on farm as well. Our certified organic feed is produced less than 50 miles away. We firmly believe in strengthening our local food system and providing our community with nutritious, organic food. Our products are sold by the share. This allows you to keep as much of the animal as possible. Pork is available by the half or whole hog. Our local butcher will custom cut your hog to your specified instructions. Chickens, turkey & quail are sold as whole birds. With the option of keeping giblets, necks, & feet to be used for dog treats, stocks and other cooking. Pre-ordering is strongly suggested. Collaborating with other small, local farms allows us to enhance our goal of bringing you closer to your farmer and the land. Our farm promotes self-sufficiency by providing a processing equipment share to community members who wish to process their own poultry. We also provide education and guidance to others who seek instruction on growing and raising food.

notes: Every business begins somewhere. However, ours began with someone in our family. My wife and I were unable to find amaranth for our sickle cell son when we settled as refugees in Seattle in October 2018. Amaranth is one of the most nutrient vegetables in Burundi and Africa in general. Thus, with the help of New Roots Seattle farm incubation programs, we started gardening our own Burundian amaranth at Hope Garden at St. Columbus Church in Kent in March 2019; and then at Mary Gay Garden in Des Moines in April 2020 after discovering the lack of local fresh organic African vegetables at the markets. So, we started selling our local fresh organic African produce at Tukwila Village Farmers’ Market for the first time. Farming being the main source of income in the majority of Burundian. Helping our mothers with their everyday farming activities when we were kids created our passion of farming. Because of the farming love and commitment, we founded our own sustainable small business “Salaam Family Farm, LLC” in 2021 when we moved to Horseneck Farm in South King County. Presently, during each Summer we spend hours enjoying, working, producing high quality local fresh organic African vegetables not only for the better life our family and African communities but also the entire South King County communities who are discovering the growth and best mixed taste of local Fresh Organic African produce from North, South, West and East Africa. We currently sell our products at the Rainier Beach Farm Stand and in the Rainier Beach Action Coalition CSA.

As friends, we spent a lot of time talking about our future, how much we love growing things, and if it was ever going to be possible to make a living farming. We decided it didn’t make sense for each of us to continue farming on our own, and instead we saw a path where we could all work together to grow more food and find more balance in our lives. In 2023, we began with one pop-up market at the Flora Bakehouse. Today, we are building on our original vision. Fruits & Veggies FC is our way of bringing a celebratory and creative spirit to our work in agriculture, teaming up to share the produce that we love, and fighting back against the isolation of farming. In some ways, Fruits & Veggies FC is similar to other farms you might be familiar with. You can get our produce through a CSA, you can find us at farmers markets, and we’re working directly with food banks and hunger relief orgs to grow vegetables for them. One of our central goals is to increase farmer pay to get closer to a living wage, and to build a farm that is sustainable for us all to work on. notes: We grow delicious, year-round ingredients and celebrate good eating in the Pacific Northwest. Our mission is to increase the variety of produce within our local community and inspire others to grow and cook their own food. We’re a small-scale farm inspired by kitchen gardens. These are backyard growing areas where home cooks grow the food they love to eat. Kitchen gardens are seasonal, diverse, experimental, and highly productive, despite their small sizes. History In January 2025, owner Michael Liang officially launched Happy Kitchen Farm. He intentionally designed a year of business experimentation where he could test different products and sales channels. Within its first month, Happy Kitchen Farm offered a spring microgreen CSA and a summer culinary herb CSA, both of which sold out within a few weeks. We created a micro farm stand on the front porch to sell any extra produce and plant starts to neighbors. notes: Love & Greens Flower Farm specializes in locally grown cut flowers in peachy corals, pinks, and sunset hues you won’t find at grocery stores or imported bouquets. Cultivating flowers on the historic Gosser property in Shelton, Washington—home to a Washington State heritage barn—we bring fresh, unique blooms to Olympia Farmers Market throughout the growing season. After 25 years in technology, I transitioned to flower farming to build something rooted in place, sustainability, and connection to our regional food system. Our bouquets range from arrangements you can afford to treat yourself with weekly to robust, opulent displays for life’s celebrations—all grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers and harvested at peak freshness just hours before market. Our flowers last all week and beyond—that’s the difference local makes. While imported blooms travel thousands of miles before reaching stores, our flowers are grown right here and ready for you at market. Our regenerative practices create vibrant habitats for beneficial insects and pollinators, with our flock of chickens providing integrated pest management to keep our growing system naturally balanced. When you choose Love & Greens Flower Farm for your home or as gifts, you’re supporting a model where local flowers, healthy ecosystems, and regional food systems bloom together. notes: BACKGROUND Tom Clark, 5th generation Sequimite co-owns and operates Clark Farms with his wife Holly. The two together have set out to provide nutritional, humane and environmentally conscious meat for their community. They have achieved this by centering their animal husbandry on preventative care and a stress free environment while preserving their family’s pristine farm for generations to come. PRACTICES Animals are rotationally grazed on the freshest most nutritious grasses and herbs keeping them healthy and fit. Tom and Holly won’t raise animals in small confinement, commercial style where disease and stress are high. They do not feed antibiotics or use added steroids or hormones to enhance their livestock. Nor do they use chemical fertilizers or pesticides on their pastures. Instead they choose a heavy hands-on approach rotating animals frequently and monitoring animal and soil health. PHILOSOPHY “Our animals are an integral part of our farming operation and livelihood so we treat them with tender loving care. They are a part of our farm’s health and they in turn help keep the soils in balance. We feel good about providing an alternative product for our community that promotes wellbeing on so many levels.” To honor the animals on the farm and to utilize as much of the animal as possible Holly has been making and selling tallow and lard soaps too for almost a decade now. name: Laughing Cows and Smiling Sheep Organic Farm LLC
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Farm Supplies; Animal Feed; Compost; Hay; Straw; Fruit & Berries; Apples; Plums/Prunes/Pluots
notes: At Laughing Cows and Smiling Sheep Organic Farm, our roots run deep in the land we care for, where nature’s balance guides everything we do. Specializing in organic hay and forage production, we are dedicated to providing the highest quality feed while nurturing the ecosystem that makes it all possible. What sets us apart is our commitment to organic practices and our respect for the land’s natural rhythms. Our fields are carefully managed without synthetic fertilizers or pesticides, allowing the grasses and legumes to grow just as nature intended. This results in nutrient-rich, clean hay and forage that animals love and thrive on. We’re fortunate to have a pristine stream that winds alongside our farm, nourishing the soil and supporting local wildlife. The presence of this waterway inspires us to prioritize soil health and conservation, ensuring our practices protect the land and water for future generations. By using natural methods to prevent erosion and enrich the soil, we ensure that the land remains fertile and vibrant. In addition to our hay fields, a small grove of apple trees adds a touch of tradition to our farm. These trees are a symbol of our dedication to sustainability and serve as a reminder of the farm’s natural abundance. The apples from these trees are not only enjoyed by us and our visitors but also by the wildlife that shares this space. We take pride in producing hay and forage that isn’t just feed, but a product of mindful stewardship and care. At Laughing Cows and Smiling Sheep Organic Farm, we believe that by working in harmony with nature, we produce not just healthy crops, but a healthier environment. Our farm is a place where tradition meets sustainability, and where every bale of hay carries the story of the land it comes from.

name: Horseshoe Bend Ranch, Inc.
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Meat & Poultry; Beef
notes: You want beef that is delicious and healthy, that came from a grower that you can trust, that was treated well, and that is delivered to your door. Horseshoe Bend Ranch provides all that with our delicious grass finished Jersey beef, raised on our thousands of acres of fields, rolling meadows, and pine and oak forests along the Little Klickitat Canyon west of Goldendale, Washington. Why Jersey? Jerseys are a smaller breed typically used for dairy, but they also taste delicious. Since they are smaller, you don’t get overwhelmed with more beef that you know what to do with, and the steaks are a healthier size. Our Jerseys are heifers (young females) and come from a large clean dairy east of Goldendale, where they have been very nicely raised and were grazing on irrigated pastures. We get them when they are culled from the dairy because are unable to get pregnant in a timely manner. They are typically 16-18 months old. They are then grass finished on a healthy diet of hay and grass pastures on our large Centerville, Washington ranch. We typically harvest our beef at about 30 to 32 months. Our beef are quickly and humanely slaughtered at a couple of different local butchers. The carcass is hung for a couple weeks in a controlled environment at the butcher to tenderize before it is cut and wrapped to your specifications. It is then frozen hard and delivered to your door. Since this is not USDA inspected we cannot charge by the cut. You are charged based on the hanging weight. Hanging weights for a half are typically between 225 and 250 pounds. We guarantee they won’t be heavier than 250 pounds or the extra is free. We also sell quarters (half of a half) and wholes for the same price per pound. We currently charge $6.00 a pound hanging weight (as of 06/2026, subject to change), and that includes everything – the beef, the kill fee, the cutting and wrapping at the butcher, and delivery to you anywhere in the Columbia Gorge, Portland, Vancouver and south to Salem, plus north to Longview. We also delivery to the Yakima Valley and the Tri-Cities, within 10 miles of the freeway. Ask about Seattle area delivery opportunities. Your total price won’t be more than $1500.00 for a half (or half that for a quarter). We will need a deposit of $200 for a half (or $100 for a quarter) to reserve your order. After slaughter we will contact you and let you know how heavy your half is, what your total cost is, and how to contact the butcher to tell them how you want your meat cut up. The butcher will walk you through the process. If there are any special cuts you want you will need to let them know at that time. If you want any organ meat let us know ahead of time when you send in your deposit as organ meats are not included in the weight. Organs are limited so they are allocated to people getting whole or half beefs first, then to quarters, and it is first deposit, first reserved. Since organs are not included in the hanging weight there is an extra charge per organ that comes to less than the hanging weight price. If there are other parts you want, ask ahead of time. We deliver to your home in person about 3 weeks after slaughter. Note that cutting and wrapping typically reduces your take-home weight by about 40-50%. Actual results vary depending on the size of your half and how you want it cut and wrapped. Typically you end up with about 1/3 steaks, 1/3 burger, and 1/3 roasts. Thanks for your interest and let us know if you have any questions or want to place an order. If you would like to come and visit our operation and meet the meat we love to welcome visitors!

name: SMR Cattle & Beef
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Eggs; Eggs (Chicken); Meat & Poultry; Beef; Livestock for Sale; Pork; Sausage; Locally Made; Local Food Box; Meal Kits; Preserved & Pantry Items; Jams & Spreads; Sauces & Condiments
notes: SMR Cattle was founded in 2018 in the heart of the Okanogan Highlands, between Molson and Chesaw, Washington. As a family-run ranch, we are passionate about raising ethically raised, grass-fed cattle with a deep commitment to both sustainability and quality. Our business began with a vision of providing beef that not only tastes exceptional but is raised with the highest ethical standards and respect for the land and animals. We take immense pride in knowing every detail about our cattle’s lives—from the pastures they graze on to the meticulous care they receive—allowing us to offer the highest quality, premium beef directly from our ranch to consumers. What truly sets us apart is our dedication to the wellbeing of our cattle, land and the community around us. We are rooted in responsible and sustainable ranching practices, where we prioritize low-stress handling, free-ranging on grass pastures, and a grass-fed approach that reflects our commitment to regenerative agriculture. We don’t cut corners, even if that means higher production costs or thinner profit margins. We believe that the quality of our beef speaks for itself. Each bite tells the story of how we care for our animals and our land, ensuring the best quality product reaches our customers’ plates. Another unique aspect of SMR Cattle is the strong community focus we bring into our operations. We’ve created a local space where ranchers and farmers can store and sell their meat through our services, acting as both a storage solution and a platform for fellow producers. We hold Rancher Socials, celebrating the hard work of local farmers and ranchers, and connect them directly with consumers through these events. Our goal is not just to sell beef but to be a resource for other local producers in our area and uplift our farming community as a whole. The connection we maintain with our customers is also key. We cater to a growing audience that wants to know where their food comes from. Through our farm-to-table operations, we provide a transparent, direct link from our pastures to their dinner tables. Whether it’s through our sales of beef shares or the “Cash Cow Club,” where customers can refer others and earn significant savings on their purchases, we strive to make our customers part of the ranching experience. We believe that when people see the dedication behind their food, they’ll appreciate it even more. SMR Cattle has big goals. We’re not just looking to grow our business; we’re building a legacy rooted in sustainable agriculture, ethical animal care, and deep community connections. One of our primary goals is to grow to a point where we can bring more of our family members into the business. We are also focused on scaling up our freezer storage capacity to support more local producers and help them get their beef to market. We envision a future where our ranch not only provides for our family but also helps other ranchers thrive and gives consumers access to more locally sourced, high-quality beef. At SMR Cattle, we don’t just produce beef—we create an experience, a connection to the land, the animals, and the people who enjoy the fruits of our labor. Every detail matters to us, and we aim to bring that care and dedication into every product we offer. Whether it’s through the flavor of our beef or the way we connect with our community, we are committed to making a difference in every aspect of our business.

notes: Our small dairy, in Zillah, is located about 20 minutes east of Yakima, WA. We milk a few Holstein cows. Our cows are registered Holsteins, and we show them at national levels. We call them “Fancy Cows”! Because of their spoiled life, our Holsteins produce high quality milk which is used to make cheese. Our cheese is made from raw milk and aged at least 60 days. The raw milk is superior in cheesemaking because the natural bacteria in the milk carries through in the aging process giving the cheese it’s unique flavors from our area. We make Gouda, Cheddar, and Butter Cheese. We also add different flavors to our Gouda cheeses. Bacon, Caraway, Peppercorn, and smoked are some of the flavors. We also have seasonal flavors too. Our beautiful Holsteins are also fed very well. They get rotational pastures most of the year. Winter time, they are fed our home grown grass hay as well as local alfalfa. Each of our cows is hand led to our parlor. Our cows love the parlor! We absolutely love our cows and love making cheese. We noticed a need for cow milk artisanal cheeses in our area. That is why we started the creamery. We hope that our community falls in love with our cheese as much as we have.

name: Red Roof Ranch
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Eggs; Eggs (Chicken); Eggs (Duck); Flowers, Nursery & Trees; Cut Flowers; Lavender; Locally Made; Home & Personal Care
notes: At the heart of the Red Roof Ranch is its expansive lavender fields that burst into a sea of vibrant purple, filling the air with a soothing fragrance that can calm even the busiest of minds. Visitors from near and far can come to stroll through the rows of lavender, picking their own bundles to take home, and enjoying the peaceful ambiance that the farm offers. But the lavender and cut flowers are just the beginning. In addition to the chickens and ducks that lay delicious eggs, the farm is a sanctuary to a variety of other animals. Horses and miniature horses grazing in the pasture, their sleek coats glistening in the sunlight. Nigerian dwarf goats, with their playful antics, bring joy to those who visit. Mini pigs, with their curious snouts will be often found rooting or enjoying a nap, while the Sebastopol geese, with their elegant white feathers, add a touch of grace to the farm’s pond. The farm is not just a place for animals and plants; it is also a vibrant community hub. The Red Roof Ranch is hosting events from weddings and family gatherings to educational tours and farm-to-table dinners. The event spaces are adorned with rustic charm which provides the perfect backdrop for creating unforgettable memories. The Red Roof Ranch is more than just a farm; it is the testament to the beauty of rural living and the joy of connecting with nature. It is the place where the simple pleasures of life can be savored and where the spirit of community thrives.

notes: Boldly Grown Farm is a certified organic family farm in Skagit Valley, WA. Established in 2015 by Amy Frye & Jacob Slosberg, we focus on wholesale production of fall and winter storage crops to provide our region with high quality, local, organic vegetables during the winter months. Specialties include radicchio, winter squash, hardy greens, watermelon, daikon radishes, beets, carrots, cabbage and more. name: Blue Glass Farm
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Fruit & Berries; Seeds & Starts; Plants/Plant Starts; Vegetable/Herb starts; Vegetables & Herbs; Asian Greens/Bok Choy; Basil; Beans (Green/Yellow); Beets; Bell peppers; Broccolini; Cabbage; Carrots; Cauliflower; Celery; Chard; Cilantro; Collard Greens; Corn; Cucumbers; Daikon; Dill; Eggplant; Fava Beans; Fennel; Garlic; Garlic Greens; Garlic Scapes; Green Onions; Herbs & Botanicals; Herbs (Fresh); Kale; Kohlrabi; Leeks; Lemongrass; Lettuce; Mustard Greens; Onions; Oregano; Parsley; Pea Vines; Peppers (Hot); Peppers (Sweet); Potatoes; Radicchio; Radishes; Root Vegetables; Salad Greens; Shallots; Sorrel; Spinach; Squash (Summer); Squash (Winter); Thyme; Tomatillos; Tomatoes; Tomatoes (Cherry); Tomatoes (Heirloom); Turnips
notes: We are Alexandra and Tyler of Blue Glass Farm. Food should be fun, and farms should protect our environment and communities; that’s why we grow 250 varieties of 80 crops using regenerative, no-till, organic farming. The two pillars of our farm are flowers and food. We love food. It’s hard to have a bad meal when you have good produce. We grow so close to the city because it means our produce can be as fresh as possible, and our customers can come out and see the quality of our operation with their own eyes. Our crop selection combines novel culinary treats like East Indian Lemongrass and interesting varieties of more familiar crops like tomatoes and greens. We want to show people that even something as seemingly bland as lettuce is available in a cornucopia of colors, textures, and flavors. Our flower operation is the newest addition to Blue Glass Farm, but it is Alex’s original passion. Many people don’t realize that the majority of flowers we buy in the Pacific Northwest come from California and Mexico and are often grown using harsh pesticides and chemicals. We grow all of our flowers just outside of Seattle without herbicides or pesticides. They’re so fresh you can eat them, which is good because we grow so many edible varieties. We thrive by serving our community. Our products go all over the Seattle area, to over 80 restaurants and food organizations, our farmer’s market stand, and through an online store where customers can pick up on the farm or receive delivery. Alex and Tyler grew up in Eastern Washington, where our parents live. Alex’s fascination with biology has always steered her towards agriculture. She pursued her undergraduate degree in biology and received a master’s in sustainable agriculture from Washington State University. During that time, she developed a small flower farm and vineyard on her parents’ property in Stevens County. She currently works at the University of Washington in the research department of the Information School. Tyler was a late convert to farming. Growing up in an agricultural community, he saw the struggle of farmers subsisting off of chemically grown, commodity agriculture. He decided to pursue a career in engineering and received a degree in mining engineering. He later discovered small-scale sustainable agriculture and fell in love with the potential for small farms to change the world. We want our farm to be a pillar of the Northshore community. We want to produce amazing food and flowers that people have never seen before, invite our community onto the farm to eat and learn, and perhaps most importantly, show by example that our green spaces are vital sources of environmental and economic sustainability. We love farming the way we do; it’s a lot of hard work, but it creates excellent products and fosters a healthy ecosystem both above and below the soil. We farm using a no-till method called deep mulching, where we use heavy applications of compost on the soil surface to suppress weeds, build soil, and feed plants through the magic of soil ecology rather than chemistry. Every tool we use is electric or human-powered. It sounds kind of crazy, but it saves us tons of money on fuel maintenance and means our farm is quiet and beautiful. Not running a tractor means we can farm more intensively, opens limitless growing options, and allows us to grow year-round, even in soggy soils.

notes: Tian Tian Farm is committed to farming with the earth in mind. We aim to minimize waste by using renewable and second-hand materials as much as possible. We also farm according to organic principles, using natural fertilizers and composts to encourage biological activity in our soil, planting herbs and flowers to attract beneficial insects, and sourcing much of our seed from certified organic producers. Tian Tian Farm seeks to promote Asian heritage vegetables in the Seattle market, both to Asian communities and to anyone else who loves to eat the food we grew up eating. We want to share our bounty of A choy, daikon, bok choy, shiso, and much more with the region’s families, chefs, and culinary adventurers. Tian Tian (天天) means “daily” in Mandarin, reminding us to take life one day at a time. Our name also reflects nature’s gentle, constant motion. We hope you can stop by our farm stand, located right next to the fields where we grow our veggies! notes: Our Heritage: Jamestown Seafood’s aquaculture practices celebrate the heritage of native S’Klallam traditions. Shellfish have been woven through the S’Klallam cultural tapestry for tens of thousands of years. S’Klallam, meaning “the strong and clever people,” coexist respectfully and responsibly, valuing the integral way that water connects villages, connects species, connects people. Along the Salish Sea – where shellfish harvesting remains a family tradition – tribes have an adage, “When the tide is out, the table is set.” Today, whether these delicacies are eaten raw, sautéed with fresh herbs, simmered into chowders, or grilled over open flame; the possibilities for our fresh, succulent seafood offerings are endless. Dive In: Spawning and early growth of our culinary treasures takes place at the tribe’s Point Whitney hatchery in Brinnon, Washington, and in Kona, Hawaii, where oyster seed is nurtured, lovingly fed algae grown on site, and bathed in constantly flowing cold, clean sea water. Later, under the veil where land and sea meets, the pristine beaches of Sequim bay and Quilcene bay provide a haven for our shellfish gems to mature. Constantly refreshed by colder currents that come in from the Pacific Ocean, the water provides ideal conditions for oysters and geoduck clams to mature. As the tides ebb and flow, waves kiss the shore and retreat again; seasons pass, and soon, this rhythmic allure of the sea beacons a harvest. The hospitality of our region’s shores yield oysters of unparalleled taste and quality. We invite you to indulge in the delicacies of our superior saltwater beds: freshly shucked, a hint of cucumber on the palate and a delicious flavor. Our Commitment: Without compromise, Jamestown Seafood’s focus is on seafood grown by people who are passionate about shellfish, throughout generation upon generation of cultural heritage and family cuisine. Every morsel has been grown and gathered with the utmost respect for our home, the Earth, and for our ancestors, our legacy. We invite you to share in enjoying the treasured bounty from our pristine saltwater beds to nourish your body and nurture your soul. Whether you need oyster seed, geoduck seed, market oysters to feature on your menu or for resale, or desire our premium farm-raised sablefish, we welcome the opportunity to work with you!

notes: EB Daniel Farm is our homestead located in Olalla Washington and established in 1994. Nestled among great Hemlock and Douglas firs our farm is a hidden paradise. We package our eggs for sales and once a week deliver our farm fresh goods to the local community. Have you ever gone to the Grocery store, looked around, and thought there had to be something better! The same boring, tasteless, mundane processed food, fruits, and vegetable all year long. Why are there so few choices in healthy food? The answer: feeding many people narrows choices and all fresh food needs to ship easy and have a long shelf life to make it across the country. Choosing to shop local means fresher produce, fruits and proteins that are unique to your area. With the invention of GMOs (Genetically modified organisms), I noticed a marked change in the growth and behavior of my livestock. They did not thrive as they did back when I was a child on the farm in the ’70s and ’80s. I did some research and found many farmers had concerns like mine. This inspired us to start growing our own food free from GMO products. Friends and family noticed the quality of our small farms produce and proteins that we soon started to produce more to provide extra for our extended family. Soon neighbors became customers and now with our delivery service, our community now has a choice of NON-GMO proteins and produce, breaking away from production farms and mega food chain stores.

notes: We operate a small regenerative farm in the Methow Valley in North-Central Washington, where we raise grass-fed lamb and cultivate hay and pasture. We use management-intensive grazing rotations to improve the soil and produce healthy animals and delicious meat. We are also engaged in restoration work on 8 acres of wooded and riparian habitat in the center of our farm. We operate our own custom butcher shop on the farm, so lamb purchased from us live their entire life on the farm and avoid the stress of travel and off-farm slaughter. We cut your meat to order, with attention to detail and a one-on-one relationship with each customer. We also sell wild sockeye salmon from our commercial fishing operation. Our fishing business (Graveyard Point Fish) is a family setnet operation on the Kvichak river in Bristol Bay. We fish from small open skiffs, pulling nets and hand-picking each fish to ensure that it is flash-frozen quickly and in good condition. The incredible Bristol Bay watershed is home to a wild sockeye population that has been steadily increasing for over 50 years. We are honored to be a part of this harvest and to bring this amazing food source to our community in Central Washington.

name: Little Dog Flower Farm
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Flowers, Nursery & Trees; Cut Flowers; Nursery Stock; Seeds & Starts; Bulbs/Tubers
notes: Little Dog Flower Farm grows dahlias and other beautiful flowers in the lovely town of Chewelah, WA. We started with the goal of growing dahlias, for both cut flowers and tuber production, but quickly fell in love with so many flowers! Every plant and flower we sell is grown right here on our land. We have always been committed to leaving our land primarily for the wildlife that calls this property home. Our farmed area has been cultivated in a very mindful way so no harm will come to the earth or the critters living within and upon it. We are a Certified Wildlife Habitat and farm with the environment at the heart of every step we take. We use no herbicides, pesticides, chemical fertilizers, and practice no tillage in our existing beds. This is our promise to Mother Nature, to honor and protect her. We are proud to be a part of the wonderful Chewelah Farmers Market, selling our locally grow cut flowers in bouquets and straight bunches, as well as dahlia starts and a small assortment of succulents. We also sell our dahlia tubers and cuttings on our website, for those outside of the Inland Northwest. Lastly, we donate a portion of all sales to a local dog rescuer here in Chewelah! Becky’s Best Buddies is a one-woman dog-saving machine and we want to support her efforts! So we like to think our flowers help save dogs!!

notes: Fabled Farms is a small-scale farm nestled in the Pend Oreille River Valley of Eastern Washington. We’re rooted in a simple belief: take care of the land, care for the animals, and provide real, honest food to our community. Sustainability isn’t a trend for us—it’s how we live and work every day. From crop rotation and composting to mindful water use and reducing waste wherever we can, we’re always working toward keeping our land healthy and productive for the long haul. We believe in using what we have well, giving back to the soil, and being good stewards of the space we’re lucky enough to call home. Our animals are raised with care, respect, and plenty of fresh air. We focus on humane practices and do not use added hormones or unnecessary antibiotics. Our goal is simple: healthy animals produce better, more nourishing food. Alongside our animals, our garden plays a big role in what we offer. We grow a seasonal variety of fruits, vegetables, and herbs using natural growing methods—skipping synthetic pesticides and fertilizers in favor of more thoughtful, earth-friendly approaches. Fabled Farms is more than just a place to buy food—it’s a connection point. Whether you find us at the farmers market or through our products, you’re supporting local agriculture, sustainable practices, and a way of life that values community, quality, and doing things the right way.

notes: Thiessen Ranch is owned by Dan & Melissa Thiessen & their sons. We aspire to produce the highest quality of beef on a small scale— crafting restaurant-quality beef from our ranch to your table. ​Our steers feed on pasture grasses carefully selected—4 varieties planted to mature throughout grazing season—for sustainable, natural energy. We constantly work to get the best result from their grain finishing—mixing 5-6 grains to produce flavorful and balanced protein and fat content. We honor how the animals digestive system appreciates macronutrients and minerals so they don’t over indulge or get sick. As a part of our closed-loop approach, we bring our steers spent grain from our brewery. Local farms nearby gives us their fruit and/or veggie surplus. You can see and taste the difference these decisions make in the quality of our beef. We carcass age before the beef is fabricated and frozen, for natural enzymes to break down the meat—resulting in a defined flavor profile that cannot truly be replicated. ​You’ll have to taste it for yourself.

Our sheep are rotationally grazed to improve our pastures and help to build the soil. In addition to pasture, lambs also have access to alfalfa hay and barley, both of which we purchase from another local Washington farm. We like to feed some grain and hay in addition to grass because it results in less gamey, more tender meat. Our breeding ewes are on pasture, eating grass only during the spring, summer, and fall months. We usually have whole and half lambs available year-round if you’re looking to stock your freezer with some delicious, humanely raised lamb meat. We also offer whole and half goats in the fall and have vegetable starts available in the spring.

name: Noordenwind Farm
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Meat & Poultry; Beef; Ground Meat; Pork
notes: When Rolf Veening decided he wanted to move to America he knew one thing to be true: he would be a farmer. Raised on a dairy farm in the northern part of the Netherlands he had an eagerness to gain farming experience in another country. Rolf explored America and found his new home in Lynden, Washington on the Vander Veen family farm. It was here that he met John Vander Veen, who would become the third generation of Vander Veen’s to run the dairy farm. T.J. Veenacre Farms is located in the upper northwest corner of Washington. Our farm located in the upper northwest corner of Washington. There you will find our picturesque farm of cedar and fir trees, where you can see the salmon spawn in the stream, green hills, and beef cows grazing their pastures. John and Rolf have been business partners since 1997, sharing their passion and skills for farming. In 2020, the farm faced a major shift when Rolf and John made the tough decision to sell the dairy cows. After a period of reflection, the farm entered an exploration phase and made a switch to start raising quality home grown beef and premium hay. Building on the success of the exploration period, Rolf started taking on the growing and marketing of the beef under a new name. 2025 marks our official rebranding of the farm as Noordenwind Farm, a tribute to Rolf’s Dutch roots. While T.J. Veenacre Farm remains the location, Noordenwind Farms represents the future of our beef farming endeavors. At Noordenwind Farm, everything is grown with patience and care. Our passion for raising animals drives our pursuit to produce the best quality product for our customers while remaining stewards of the land, therefore creating a lasting difference in our community.

notes: Snipes Mountain Ranch was born from our desire to build a relationship with those who appreciate fresh, local and responsibly-raised produce and beef. Our products have historically been sold through the traditional produce distribution channels (farm to packing house to grocery store). Lost in those logistics, however, is the connection between the farmer and consumer. We constantly strive for the highest quality, only sending the best to market, but it wasn’t until we expanded to offer direct-to-consumer that we experienced the satisfaction of seeing our products bring happiness, health, and enjoyment to the people that purchased them. Seasonal Products We offer cherries and certified organic pears when they are fresh off the tree. This is typically around July for cherries and August/September for pears, but is ultimately up to Mother Nature. You can pre-order to ensure that you get our fresh, delicious fruit first or sign-up for our mailing list to know when cherries and pears will be available. Year Round Products We have our beef year round! You have a choice of selecting a crate of pre-selected items or individual cuts based on your desire.

name: McFarland Creek Lamb Ranch
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Meat & Poultry; Lamb; Locally Made; Yarn, Fiber & Wool
notes: McFarland Creek Lamb Ranch is a small sheep ranch in the beautiful Methow Valley in North Central Washington State. We raise Romney and Cormo sheep for both fiber and meat. Our philosophy is to use the least invasive and most humane methods possible. Our flock is rotated through several fenced pastures, which are irrigated with gravity fed water from the creek. In the winter, the flock feeds on local alfalfa hay. We hand pull weeds in order to avoid using herbicides, and use pasture rotation to control parasites and allow the grass to have periods of restoration throughout the growing season. We live on the edge of wilderness, so predators are an issue. We are committed to a live and let live philosophy, so have invested in secure fencing and a team of Livestock Guardian Dogs (LGDs) to protect the flock. We sell meat direct market to our customers, who can purchase a whole or half lamb. Customers can pick up locally or we can deliver to the greater Seattle area by appointment. We wash our wool by hand, and dye it with natural dyes, some of which are grown on the ranch, and some purchased from a reputable Fair Trade supplier. It is then sent out for spinning at a small family run mill (Spinderellas) to be made into roving and yarn. Each fleece is processed separately, so you always know which sheep your yarn came from.

products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Flowers, Nursery & Trees; Cut Flowers; Edible Flowers; Lavender; Nursery Stock; Fruit & Berries; Strawberries; Vegetables & Herbs; Asian Greens/Bok Choy; Beets; Broccoli; Carrots; Cucumbers; Pea Vines; Peas; Pumpkins; Squash (Summer); Squash (Winter); Tomatoes; Tomatoes (Cherry); Tomatoes (Heirloom)
notes: WA Hmong Farmers Cooperative (WHFC): We are a collective of direct market growers in the Hmong Community who have been selling products at Pike Place Market and the region’s farmers markets since 1982. We have created this Cooperative to increase access to our products for anyone interested in beautiful flowers and fresh produce. WHFC Mission: The Mission of WHFC is to provide WA state and other communities with direct access to locally produced foods and flowers while supporting the sustainability of our local Hmong farms and preserving their Hmong farming tradition. About the Hmong farmers: The story of Hmong farmers in the Downtown Seattle and the Puget Sound Region is a testament to the resilience and hard work of the Hmong farming community. As Vietnam War refugees arriving in the United States in the 1970s, members of the Hmong community brought their agricultural expertise, which allowed them to establish livelihoods as farmers. In 1982, the Indochinese Farm Project was initiated with funding from King County, the Pike Place Market Preservation and Development Authority, and Washington State University. Starting with only six families, the project grew over the years to support more than 80 families. Through this project, Hmong farmers were introduced to floriculture. They quickly embraced this opportunity and became specialists in flower farming. Their efforts resulted in stunning flower displays at Pike Place Market, which have become a major tourist attraction all year round. This has had a substantial economic impact on the Puget Sound Region and Downtown Seattle, attracting visitors and supporting local businesses. In 2022, the establishment of the Washington Hmong Farmers Cooperative (WHFC) with 14 Hmong farms marks a significant milestone for the Hmong farming community. As the first Hmong farmer-owned cooperative in the United States, WHFC plays a vital role in supporting Hmong farmers and addressing the challenges they face. This cooperative has become especially important to help farmers recover after significant financial losses they experienced during the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020 when regional farmers markets were closed. The WHFC helps Hmong farmers reach customers beyond traditional farmers markets by connecting them to a diverse range of buyers, such as other cooperatives, restaurants, hospitals, grocery stores, schools, food banks, and nonprofits. This not only diversifies their sales avenues but also ensures a more stable source of income for the Hmong farmers. Furthermore, the WHFC invests in the continuation of the Hmong farming tradition, which has become an integral part of the Puget Sound Region’s culture and economy. Coop Members Include (as of August 2023): *True garden *Thao Flowers *Yeng’s Flowers *Chou Valley Fresh *Flower Garden *Petals and Stems *The Old Farmer *Kia’s Garden *Younique Garden *Lee’s Fresh Produce *Thai D Garden *Chong Floral Bouquet

notes: The Pickering family has owned and operated Novelty Hill Farm since 1884. Originally a dairy farm, we now produce pumpkins, hay, and a variety of vegetables. Open to the public only seasonally, but we offer private venue rentals in our barns for your gatherings year-round! We offer U-pick blackberries in August- wild blackberry bushes abound on our farm, and they produce the yummiest fruit! We do not use herbicides or pesticides, so you can rest assured that you are getting the best and healthiest fruit possible. Fall is the best time of year on the farm, and we like to celebrate with family fun for everyone! We offer Fall Fun Fest during October: a pumpkin patch, corn maze, trike track, hay mow, corn crib, farm critters, snacks, and gathering spaces for your party! Come visit us and join in the farm experience! Free admission and dog-friendly (on leash). We also sell pre-cut Christmas trees for a roughly ten-day season after Thanksgiving. Come enjoy some hot cocoa while you explore our 1930’s barns, shop local arts and crafts vendors, and find your perfect tree! We offer wreaths, swags, garland, Christmas decorations, and more! name: Holy Cow Better Beef
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Meat & Poultry; Beef; Ground Meat
notes: At Holy Cow Better Beef it’s the grass that makes our beef better. We utilize ONLY the natural and sustainable resources that God has blessed us with to provide you with the lean healthy nourishment that all-natural grass-fed, grass-finished beef can offer. Our Angus cross cattle have been selectively bred to thrive in a grass and plant-based environment. The high elevations and abundant fresh water of the Kettle River Range in NE Washington provide ideal summer pasture for cattle to develop naturally on lush native grasses and plants. The temperate climate of the Palouse River Valley in SE Washington allows grazing throughout the winter on native grass range. When winter conditions necessitate, HCBB cattle are supplemented with a mixture of quality hay from local producers. Our cattle handling and processing is done traditionally utilizing the low stress connections among cattle, horses, and humans. Our commitment to providing NO ANTIBIOTIC, NO HORMONE, NATURAL grass-finished beef is one we do not take lightly. Start to finish, “A cow raised the way God intended, makes better beef”. Beyond the beef, HCBB is built on rich ranching traditions and respect for God, people, livestock, and land. At HCBB we resonate with Winston Churchill when he said “There is nothing better for the inside of a man than the outside of a horse.” And so we invest in the next generation by offering a faith- and character-based ranch internship program. Our mission is to build character while teaching horsemanship and low-stress livestock handling. We utilize the agricultural setting and a whole, healthy lifestyle to encourage and develop the minds, hearts, and souls of young people. We are what we eat. And what we eat is more than just the food that goes into our mouths, it is the process and people who bring that food to our tables. Invest in sustainable, healthy food today and reap the blessing for years to come.

name: bedhead fiber
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Seeds & Starts; Locally Made; Yarn, Fiber & Wool
notes: bedhead fiber is a declaration of adoration for plants, fungi, natural fibers, farmers, the slow process. We believe in the power of plants, the necessity of healthy ecosystems, and supporting farmers. bedhead fiber is grateful to live and work on Duwamish land. We appreciate the long, slow process, and things that ask us to pause. If we respect where things come from and their lives, how they grow, we in turn respect what they have to offer. We source fiber from US grown and milled farms, primarily based out of the Pacific Northwest. Most of the dye materials have been hand foraged by our team or traded with other foraging friends all with sustainability in mind–ethically harvesting and foraging, and often growing our own dye materials. We supplement raw material dyes with extracts sourced directly from the farmers. bedhead fiber products are a commitment to sustainability, healthy ecosystems, and strong communities. We believe that the yarn and textiles we create are not only beautiful, but hold intention and value to the fiber, farmer, and foraging communities.

name: Salt Blade
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Locally Made; Preserved & Pantry Items; Fermented Foods
notes: At Salt Blade we believe in direct support of sustainable farming practices. All of the meat we use comes from Olsen Farms in Colville, WA. In addition to growing the finest potatoes in the Northwest, the Olsen family raises Berkshire, Duroc, and Tamworth pigs that feed on the barley that grows abundantly on their land. They also keep a herd of 100% grass fed cows. Though not certified organic, they use only organic practices. Once the meat arrives in Seattle we aggressively lean it out and grind it. We then gently mix it with the carefully measured spices, fresh ingredients, and curing salts. We hand stuff and hand link the salamis, as has been done for centuries. Fermentation takes place in a carefully controlled environment before the dry curing finishes in our curing chamber. We hope you enjoy the results!

notes: At Ecolibrium, we grow certified organic produce, and adhere to the principles of regenerative agriculture. We are driven by market gardening principles, utilizing human-scale tactics and keeping a light footprint, as we produce a large quantity of quality produce on small acreage, using ecologically-sound practices. We started Ecolibrium because we believe that growing food in an ecologically-sound manner enhances the health and vitality of our natural ecosystems. While our focus is on growing produce, the principles we employ in our field support the larger ecosystem within which we farm. These principles are rooted in a profound reverence and fascination with the natural world, and the belief that the more diverse the land is the more resilient the farm can be. Our guiding principles include: – Certified organic – WSDA and The Real Organic Project – Permanent beds to help increase soil health – Dynamic Pest Management – Low-till, low disturbance soil practices to enhance the biodiversity of the soil – Targeted fertilization with granular organic amendments, reducing run-off into local waterways – Keeping the edges of the field wild so beneficial, birds, insects and fungi can have habitat We grow diversified vegetables on our 2+ acre, organic farm in Redmond, WA.

notes: My husband Drew and I (Jen) began our farm in 2002 in Buckley, Wa. We fell in love with the land situated with a view of Mt. Rainier and the cascade foothills. We began cultivating the soils by growing winter squash for the Root Connection Farm in Woodinville Wa. The Root Connections is one of the oldest CSA farms in our nation owned by my mother Claire Thomas. With her guidance and expertise we launched our own farm here following the same growing methods and business model. Over the years we have learned much about what grows well here and what we need to bring in from other farms which help build connection and allow diversity in the produce our members receive. Discover how you and your family can eat healthier, tastier produce while at the same time helping to preserve small local farming in our area. Everything is grown in a manner that is safer for the earth and the people who eat from it. Our produce will be ‘taking root’ on several different local farms who share the same passion for healthy, organic growing practices. This will allow us to bring our members a weekly box that is more diversified week to week. By supporting TRF and the farms they partner with our members will ensure healthy farmlands for future generations. Members will benefit by receiving the freshest, tastiest, most nourishing produce available. When members arrive, their box is already packed with a variety of fresh seasonal fruits and vegetables. Members enjoy all the fruits of our labor without all the work! Members also have the option of adding u-pick items such as greens, herbs and flowers as they are in season to their box. name: Vale Creek Farm
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Eggs; Eggs (Chicken); Meat & Poultry; Beef
notes: Vale Creek Farm is a small family farm. Our goal is to provide the local community with the best possible meat, eggs, and produce, while implementing regenerative and ethical farming practices. After years of dreaming of having our own farm, we finally found the perfect place with an old farmhouse in the summer of 2020. Since then we have been building livestock fences, clearing out brambles, and rejuvenating neglected pastures. We welcomed our first small cattle herd to the farm in 2021 and our cows have had 3 calves since. In March on 2022 we started with day old chicks to raise as laying hens, which are now pasture raised in an egg mobile built on an old 24-ft trailer frame. Eggs are now available to purchase on farm at our farmstand. Agroforestry is another extensive project we have implemented on the farm. Nut trees have been started from seed and planted throughout the pastures including oak, walnut, chestnut, and hazelnut. These trees will give shade for grass and livestock, produce nut crops, and create an ecosystem for diverse wildlife.

name: Filaree Fruit
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Fruit & Berries; Apples; Apricots/Apriums; Nectarines; Peaches; Pears (Asian); Plums/Prunes/Pluots; Vegetables & Herbs; Garlic; Garlic Greens; Garlic Scapes
notes: Filaree Fruit stands as a small yet diverse orchard perched on a land bench above the Okanogan River valley. Boasting over 30 years as a certified organic farm, Filaree has nurtured rich living soil and flourishing, robust trees. Spanning ten acres, Filaree Fruit employs a unique approach to cultivation—a variation of swidden agriculture. This method involves long rotations of fruit, nut, and shelter trees, punctuated by shorter periods of use as smaller garden plots and pastures. Over the years, this system has proven highly effective, yielding commercially viable quantities of marketable crops. Beyond the commercial aspect, it mimics the benefits of a forest, providing a pleasant habitat for humans and animals, a sustainable source of firewood and lumber, and local climate moderation. Notably, the system also prioritizes soil health, enhancing organic matter and fostering soil life—a cornerstone of Filaree Fruit’s sustainable practices. Filaree Fruit is a treasure trove for apple enthusiasts, offering a diverse selection of over 30 heirloom varieties. The apple season kicks off in mid-July with Vista Bellas, Nickajacks, and King Davids, progressing through late summer with Winesaps and Arkansas Blacks, and extending into the late fall. Peaches take center stage from mid-July through September, accompanied by the delightful presence of nectarines and several plum varieties. Since 2010, Filaree Fruit has been under the ownership and care of JC and Amber Kauffman, alongside their daughter Hazel. Committed to upholding the farm’s tradition, they infuse joy into the art of tending to the orchard, ensuring that the legacy of growing beautiful and diverse fruit remains alive and vibrant.

The berries were planted more than 80 years ago – likely in the late 1930’s or early 1940’s. Each variety has a different size and flavor, from small and sweet to big and tart. To care for the berries, use sustainable practices. We seek to be a mindful part of our watershed that ultimately feeds into the Snoqualmie River and the Salish Sea. Uniquely sited in the woods near Duvall, Washington, you’ll come for the blueberries but might get a chance to enjoy nature, including towering evergreens, curious deer, singing birds and more. In addition to blueberries, we offer u-pick and we-pick flower bouquets. You can round out your trip by purchasing local products including honey (from bees on our farm!), jams made from our blueberries, and other goods from local partners. We also offer an adults only “Date Night” on Saturday evenings, where guests can enjoy the company of a significant other (or friend, or whatever!) while enjoying nibbles from our farm and partner producers and picking berries. name: Browning Beef LLC
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Meat & Poultry; Beef
notes: At Browning Ranch: We believe the well being of the earth and our animals is paramount. We have a “closed herd” meaning, all of our cattle are raised from birth on our ranch. They are pasture raised and are grass fed and finished. None of them ever receive any grain, corn, soy, or wheat bi-product. Over 5,000 acres of land are owned/leased for pasture. Our entire herd winters down on the Snake River where they continue to roam and graze on grass; as well as hay and alfalfa. The milder climate is ideal for our calving mama cows. We vaccinate twice a year for protection from disease. No hormones or antibiotics are ever used. We never spray for weeds as our rotational grazing practices over the years have naturally managed the land. We are passionate about the environment and its growth and protection, hence our regenerative grazing practices as well as the creating and maintaining ecosystems on our pastures. We feel strongly about providing a high quality product for the betterment of all.

name: Food Bank Growers
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Eggs; Eggs (Chicken); Eggs (Duck); Vegetables & Herbs
notes: The Food Bank Growers network grows, gathers, and gives organically grown fruits and vegetables to build healthy, vibrant communities, improve food security, and decrease food waste for our Jefferson County neighbors. Our gardens and website will provide “how-to” knowledge for best practices and be gathering spots for collaboration and fostering other food network connections. The Food Bank Garden Network is built upon these core beliefs: That consistent access to adequate daily nutrition is a fundamental human right. That by using an educational approach to gardening, volunteers can use learned skills in their own gardens and feel enriched in their volunteer experience. That by gathering (gleaning) unused produce from our neighbors, their gardens are healthier, there is more available to feed our community, and food is kept out of the waste stream. That fresh, organic produce can actively support healthier communities, contributing to lower incidence of lifestyle-related chronic diseases, such as obesity and diabetes. That by working together, we can accomplish more than by working separately. That there is ample abundance in Jefferson County sufficient to nurture and sustain all of us. That sharing good food brings joy and builds good relationships. Nourishing the soil, nourishes the plants that grow in it and in turn they nourish us.

notes: Okanogan Producers Marketing Association (OPMA) is a cooperative of six small family farms working together in the Okanogan Valley in North Central Washington State. Our six farms include Apple Cart Fruit, Bunny Laine Fruit, Filaree Fruit, Grandpa’s Homeplace, M & A Orchards, and Whitestone Mountain Orchard. OPMA Farms grow and market Washington State Department of Agriculture Certified Organic. Established in 2006, OPMA has since built strong connections with our valued customers, earning a well-deserved reputation for delivering exceptional fruit quality, outstanding customer service, and reliable shipments. The naturally warm and sunny climate in the Okanogan creates an ideal environment for producing the highest quality fruit globally! Our emphasis lies in crop diversification to create habitats for wildlife, safeguard biodiversity, and fortify climate resilience. This commitment translates into OPMA boasting a broad and diverse range of products. Consider our 2.5-acre plot with over 25 heirloom varieties and another farm cultivating 57 different varieties, encompassing 14 types of apples, all within an 11-acre space.
