notes: Blue Ridge Farm is a regenerative farm and plant nursery on 81 acres of pasture and timber. The farm is located in the beautiful Aladdin Valley, just north of Colville, and is unique for its ongoing commitment to wildlife conservation and land stewardship. No harmful chemicals No tilling No synthetic fertilizers The farm offers seasonal produce as well as a wide assortment of heirloom and open-pollinated vegetable plants, trees, shrubs, and perennials for the northern garden and greenhouse. Nearly all of our plants are grown from seed – no grafting – because we believe in celebrating the genetic diversity and unique characteristics that seed-grown propagation can bring. notes: At Fresh Nature, we live at the crossroads where tradition and innovation intersect. Beginning as a small family farm dating back over four generations in the Pacific Northwest, we have transformed from general commodity producers into a vertically integrated production company pushing the boundaries for how chickpeas are taken to market. Fresh green chickpeas have long been known as a seasonal delicacy throughout the world, and Fresh Nature has emerged as the first company in North America to bring these fresh picked, young green chickpeas to market in an frozen format. We grow, mechanically harvest and shell, then IQF process our green chickpeas. This allows us to not only provide year round supply but also lock in the vibrant bright green color and maximize nutritional value, making green chickpeas the newest superfood available to consumers around the globe.

Owner operator Kia Armstrong has been farming since 2003, and helped managed Nash’s Organic Produce for 15 years before starting her own farm. notes: Our roots go back to the logging boom of the early 1900s. During the wet and soggy winter months when conditions impeded local forestry work, many men were left unemployed. Andrew Johnson & his son-in-law Charlie Sr. Gunstone capitalized on this untapped workforce and hired them to harvest clams. After over 100 years, the farm’s headquarters remain on the shores of Discovery Bay and business has evolved to include oysters. Brothers Reed Jr. and Andrew are the 5th generation to work the farm alongside their father, Reed Sr. Mostly we sell commercially, but during the spring and fall we run our Farm Drop program. Our super fresh oysters, clams, and other seasonal items are dropped off at our regional partners in coolers straight from the farm. Customers arrive during a pickup window on drop day and are greeted by a J&G Shellfish Ambassador who will distribute the products.

name: Emerson Gardening Services
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Flowers, Nursery & Trees; Edible Flowers; Native Plants; Nursery Stock; Trees; Seeds & Starts; Bulbs/Tubers; Plants/Plant Starts; Vegetable/Herb starts; Vegetables & Herbs; Arugula; Basil; Chives; Herbs & Botanicals; Salad Greens; Sorrel
notes: WHAT WE GROW We specialize in growing Western Washington native plants, medicinal and culinary herbs, many of which are rare and/or endangered. Some of the most popular native plants we sell include oxalis, yellow glacier lily, wild ginger, yellow stream violet, Western bleeding heart, and evergreen huckleberry. Some of the most popular culinary or medicinal herbs we sell include Tea plants (Camellia sinensis), wasabi (the true wasabi, not horseradish), Tulsi basil, Valerian, Goldenseal, and Black Cohosh. BACKGROUND We have been growing plants on our 3.5 acre Vashon property for 17 years. We are growing over 265 species of plants here, nearly all in full or part shade. The property has been spray free since 2003. DIRECT SALE PRICES – including tax 3.5-5 inch pots: $7 5.5-8 inch pots: $14 9-11 inch pots: $21 12-14 inch pots: $29 HOW TO PURCHASE Our retail nursery is not open to the public. We sell at the Vashon Farmer’s Market in April and May, and then once a month in June, July, August, September, and October. We also sell plants by special arrangement, with pickup only (not shopping), at our nursery. When the Farmer’s Market is running, you can see what we have for sale at www.SourceWhatsGood.com, and either order there or through us directly. At other times you can see our list of available plants at https://www.emersongardening.com/plants-for-sale. If you don’t see what you are looking for, please contact us. We have many more plants than what we list. MEDICINAL PLANTS Michael Laurie is the medicinal plant expert on our team. Our property is a registered Medicinal Botanical Sanctuary, through United Plant Savers. It is listed under Dragonfly Medicinals. https://unitedplantsavers.org/bsn-member-directory/ We also have guidance for growing medicinal and other plants on two websites: Watershed LLC’s site: https://www.watershedllc.net/medicinal-herbs. and Garden Green: https://www.gardengreen.org/ For more information on the medicinal plants we recommend downloading the iPlant app to your smart phone. For each plant it has photos and great information on range and appearance, parts used, physiological effects, medicinal uses, culinary uses, constituents, contraindications, and more. We have over 70 books on herbs. Michael has read every page of over half of them. Out of all those books, Michael has two books on herbs that he recommends: “Medicinal Plants of the Pacific West” by Michael Moore, not the filmmaker, but a no longer living but outstanding genius herbalist. Also, there is the web site for the Herbalism school that he founded which has a lot of free medicinal herb information. I recommend anything you find there written by Michael Moore. I was lucky enough to see him at an Herb Conference in Oregon about 20 years ago and he held his own very well on a panel with MD doctors as far as his understanding of physiology, microbiology, anatomy, and healing. https://www.swsbm.com/HOMEPAGE/HomePage.html Another good herb book is the National Geographic “Guide to Medicinal Herbs”. Two of the authors are MD doctors and the four authors are all top herbal medicine experts. And most of what they say is backed up by scientific studies. And it is only 6 years old, so it is pretty up-to-date on a lot of the latest studies and research. Some of you may not be familiar with what the typical pricing is for medicinal plants and seeds. To see what prices one of the other sellers of medicinal plants and seeds is charging we recommend that you visit the site of Strictly Medicinal Seeds. https://strictlymedicinalseeds.com/ As you will see their prices are the same as ours except that we don’t have a shipping or handling fee. And with us you get the benefit of our over 20 years of growing medicinal plants on Vashon. We know which medicinals are easy or not so hard to grow here and which ones can be challenging. And our seeds are from plants that we have been growing on Vashon for many years. NATIVE PLANTS Our Pacific Northwest native plants are vitally important to native insects and birds. We are propagating them from our own stock, and a few we have added from other local suppliers of native plants. It is a joy to go for a walk in our mixed deciduous and evergreen forest, and see wild ginger, inside-out flower, native bleeding heart, false lily of the valley, trillium, trout lily, and many more shade tolerant and beautiful native plants. We recommend reading Professor Doug Tallamy’s books to really understand the importance of native plants for the future of our wildlife in North America. Here is what he has to say about it: “Unless we modify the places we live, work, and play to meet not only our own needs but the needs of other species as well, nearly all species of wildlife native to the United States will disappear forever. This is not speculation. It is a prediction backed by decades of research on species-area relationships by ecologists who know of what they speak. And the extinction of our plants and animals is not a scenario lost in the distant future. It is playing out across the country and the planet as I write.” Doug Tallamy. https://homegrownnationalpark.org/tallamys-hub-1 GARDEN GREEN Michael Laurie has been educating the community on the harm of toxic pesticides for many years, and Diane Emerson joined him in this work in 2014. Together, with other community support, we run Garden Green. Over the years Michael and Diane have helped our retailers switch to safer products to address gardening challenges, and given many talks to the community. We have many resources to people on our website: https://www.gardengreen.org/

notes: De La Mesa Farms is a family-owned 2.5 acre farm located in the urban setting of Tacoma, Washington. Our farm is a regenerative, no-till market garden that focuses on organic methods to improve soil health and soil biodiversity. We are committed to being good stewards of the land and think about farming as a way to preserve and perpetuate our own cultural heritage as well as the various BIPOC traditions in our community. Our mission is to offer fresh, diverse and affordable produce. Despite the fact that everything is done by hand – no tractor, no till – we are always seeking ways to innovate and usher in a new generation of farmers. We use hyrdroponic/aquaponic systems to grow our microgreens, cultivate mushrooms and other row crops are grown in the ground. We brew our own compost tea to improve soil conditions and diversify the microbes in the soil. We inoculate our beds with various mycelium to create symbiotic relationships with plant root systems. We pasture raise our poultry. Our farm is focused on growing unique and heirloom vegetables with a Latin and subtropical twist such as dried Oaxacan corn, smoky peppers, yuzu and much more. Owners Bryan and Natalie Mesa originally began farming in Waimanalo, Hawaii in 2016. In 2020, amidst the pandemic, they took a leap of faith and purchased land in Tacoma, Washington to relaunch their farm in the Pacific Northwest. Bryan and Natalie are farmers first, but they are also working on offering farm to table value-added products such as fiery salsas, pickles, ferments and freshly prepared masa and tortillas from the heirloom dried corn they grow on their farm. When Bryan and Natalie initially began farming in Hawaii, they did so because they couldn’t find fresh Latin produce to make the home-cooked Mexican meals that Bryan grew up on. Bryan’s family is from Mexico and he spent much of his youth in Michocan, Mexico learning to cook from his abuelita. They are excited about sharing their products with customers when they become available in the Spring of 2023. .

The Grainery is committed to increasing access to whole grain nutrition, to building health in our soils and to growing resilience and vitality in our regional foodshed. The Grainery offers organic grains and stone-milled flours, rustic pastas, and baked goods for retail and wholesale. Future plans include floor malting and brewing!

notes: Started in 1991, Persephone Farm unfolds across a sunny 6.5 acre slope in Indianola. We are passionate about the exceptional freshness and quality of the produce and flowers we offer as well as about our connections with the community. Wedding and event flowers are a specialty of ours. We are proud to be a Farm to Food Bank contributor. Owner, Rebecca Slattery, has trained over 50 future farmers through her well-respected, often life changing 8 month internship program. All practices are compliant with National Organic standards, though we are not certified organic. We like the terms regenerative or “morganic” to sum up our principles of sustainability and environmental stewardship. Priorities for Persephone include minimizing landfill- bound waste through closed loop systems, making our own compost, and providing food and habitat for bees and other pollinators by integrating flowers throughout our fields and incorporating wildland buffers on the perimeters. We employ low-til practices to sequester soil carbon and enhance soil health. There is a lot of love in our food and flowers, and we believe our customers can feel and taste this.

The word “Chesed” is defined as: Lovingkindness, the idea of faithful love in action and often in the refers to God’s lovingkindness expressed in His covenant relationship with His people. God’s chesed-love denotes persistent and unconditional tenderness, kindness, and mercy, a relationship in which He seeks after man with love and mercy. This captures the spirit of why we operate a local farm. To show love to our neighbors and community through providing nutritious, healthy, conscious food. When the mushrooms are done fruiting, the left over material is composted and made available as a soil amendment. name: Vashon Garlic
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Vegetables & Herbs; Garlic
notes: Located on Vashon Island, we are a family owned small farm committed to sustainable farming practices. Not only are we certified organic, but we are working to increase the vitality of our soil with permaculture methods in mind. Over the next few years we are transitioning to no-till farming. This will improve soil health, increase yield, and develop a sustainable ecosystem full of biodiversity. Our heirloom variety of softneck garlic is unique to our farm. It was originally brought to Dockton in the early 20th century when our neighbor, Mande Roncevich, immigrated from Croatia for an arranged marriage. Among her possessions were a few heads of garlic from her small town, enough to start a small crop. In 1983, when Mande was too old to farm, our family was sold the stock and began selling at Pike Place Market. Our variety quickly became known to be high quality and soon gained recognition by Arthur Schwartz, The Food Maven. Many years later, we are expanding and reinvigorating the farm, continuing to cultivate the best garlic available.

notes: We are a small farm offering diverse vegetables. We use organic practices to grow lettuce, kale, Swiss chard, collards, carrots, beets, radishes, turnips, peas, tomatoes, squash, and more! Because of our deep reverence for the land that feeds us and gives us a home, we choose growing practices that are ecological and sustainable. -We choose to use regenerative farming methods. Farming can be intense! On the land, that is. We use regenerative methods, such as cover cropping, diverse plant species, and responsible animal grazing, to grow abundant food that also enriches the land. -We choose to not till our soil in order to support a thriving soil food web; this allows the real heroes: the macro and microogranisms, fungi and bacteria, to live in a harmonious ecosystem with plant life. Not tilling builds lots of organic matter in the soil, sequestering carbon and storing it there. Tillage is responsible for a significant amount of atmospheric carbon while also degrading soil structure (think 1930s dust bowl), so unfortunately that means that even organic farms that utilize tillage can be causing environmental harm. We are also the first, and so far, the only farm on the Olympic Peninsula to receive the status of Certified Naturally Grown. This means that we adhere to responsible growing practices free from pesticides and herbicides, and we use only organic amendments, most of which are produced on the farm. Our farmstand is Pay What You Can so anybody can have access to local and nourishing fruits and vegetables. If you can pay more to assist your neighbors, please do, but never let the price of our food stop you from purchasing. There are suggested prices on all of our products, but pay what you can! We accept cash, check, Venmo, and PayPal.

name: Heartwood Nursery

notes: Heartwood Nursery is a small-scale bare root fruit and nut tree nursery. Our trees are grown sustainably, propagated by hand, with love in Port Townsend, Washington. ​ Bare Root Basics No plastic pots means we sell our trees “bare root”. At Heartwood Nursery, trees are grown in deeply mulched permanent beds. These require zero plastic pots and dramatically less water to stay happy. Deep mulch also transforms into vibrantly rich soil that feeds the plants. Bare root trees can only be dug and sold during the dormant season (late fall to early spring). This is when the trees are asleep and can be transplanted with the least disruption possible. Trees planted this way are less prone to transplant shock. They will have a better start in their first season, being watered in with winter rains before waking up in their new home. Bare root trees require us to deliberately plan our plantings around the dormant season. Plants available December 2023 – April 2024, or until sold out.

notes: Certified organic provider of wine and table grapes. Organic winemaking starts in the vineyard. This region is ideal for achieving that perfect chemistry needed for good fruit and good wine, because it is so consistently windy and dry. As far as flavor profiles, there is a much stronger fruit presence and vibrancy to organic wine. During maceration, the temperature is kept lower, which helps preserve those varietal-specific characteristics. Although for most red wines, age-ability is desirable, organic red wines walk the line between that naturally occurring youthfulness and fresh vibrancy and preserving the wine against that oxygen constraint.

Our flagship winery and production facility is 15,000 square feet, which includes a 13,500 square foot cellar, tank, warehouse and barrel area as well as a 1,500 square foot tasting room, gift shop and office. Great wine can only come from great fruit, that coupled with a state-of-the-art production facility means we have the perfect opportunity to make amazing wines. We opened our doors as a 3,000 case winery and are now at approximately 35,000 cases.

notes: Since 1932 the Gordon Family has been farming in the Skagit Valley. Located in the Pacific Northwest, the farm lies in a delta created over eons by the Skagit River. The loamy soil from the river’s deposits and marine climate makes it ideal to grow a variety of crops. Our location in the central part of the valley gives us surrounding views, mountains, snow capped volcanoes and sunsets. The Gordon Family has dedicated itself to the intuition of agriculture believing in its rich history and its important future to feed us – mind, body and soul. In the autumn season we open our doors to all those who venture forth and reward our visitors with good value and simple honest fun. We grow and sell carving and cooking pumpkins, heirloom and specialty pumpkins. Pick your own or choose from our bountiful autumn market display. Our winter squash are vine ripe in a wide selection of sizes, shapes, varieties and colors; they are both delicious to eat and beautiful to behold. Gourds, corn stalks and ornamental corn will round out your fall decor. Jonagold apples hang from our trees, ripe for your picking or from bins in our heritage barn. Our locally-pressed cider is a refreshing fall treat. , The Crop Circle corn maze and All-Hallow-Even-in-the-Back-of-the-Barn are festive and fun traditions that are free of charge to our pumpkin customers. On weekends in October the Red Fox Cider Shack is open for hot cider and tasty baked treats with proceeds benefiting the LaConner High School Culinary Arts Program., Unique to Gordon Skagit Farms are large original paintings of Skagit Valley farm scenes which act as a backdrop for our autumn marketplace. Limited edition posters of selected artworks are available for sale each year.

notes: Welcome to Mt. Pleasant Iris Farm, home of Chad Harris and Dale Grams, as well as the site of a national display garden of Japanese Iris. Over the years Chad and Dale have been selecting for show-quality cut blooms and plants that are more disease resistant in the Columbia River Gorge (USDA zone 8.), Chad has been growing and hybridizing Iris ensata (Japanese Iris) for over 25 years. Currently he has also started to work with Iris laevigata and a new hybrid to the world involving Iris pseudacorus x Iris ensata called a Pseudata. Look for new introductions of these varieties in the near future., Chad is member of the American Iris Society and several sub chapters of that society. He also serves as a master judge and is an active member of the Greater Portland Iris Society., Our peak iris family bloom is extended over a three month period, April-June. To help you figure out when an iris will bloom for you, these months also correlate with the peak bloom of Narcissus (April), Peonies (May), and Daylilies (June.), You and your family are also invited to visit the gardens. Located in the scenic Columbia Gorge, the public is invited to view Mt. Pleasant Iris Farm. Click here to see garden hours, directions and a map to the farm.

notes: SkyRoot Farm is a 20 acre, certified organic, farm on the east side of South Whidbey Island. We follow an ecosystems approach to farming and carry regenerative agriculture ideals through all that we do. Our fields consist of a constantly changing patchwork of diversified vegetables. We use no pesticides or herbicides on our crops, and when weeds are present we pull them the old fashioned way. notes: SpringRain Farm & Orchard is a 28-acre certified organic family farm located in the heart of Chimacum. The co-owners, John Bellow and Roxanne Hudson, have worked with their farm team to develop an ecologically-based diversified production system. We grow orchard fruit and raise 10 different kinds of berries along with mixed salad greens, tomatoes, peppers, and winter greenhouse production. We also focus on producing ethically-raised protein and raise chickens, ducks, and rabbits. We have integrated conservation hedgerows and riparian buffers throughout the farm to provide habitat for lots of birds, reptiles, amphibians, and native pollinators. SpringRain Farm & Orchard is unique because of our focus on season extension and out of season production. Our growing strategies complement other growers because we emphasize the production of crops when they are not normally being produced. We are focused on reducing our carbon footprint through carbon sequestration, geothermal earth-sheltered greenhouses, and our 9.8 kW solar array that produces electricity for the farm. Using unheated greenhouses lets us produce food year round for the local community, which means the local community has access to organic, healthy food raised locally at a time when most produce is shipped in. Our products are available at our on-farm farm stand open 7 days a week during the daylight hours. Self-Service Honor System.

notes: Jardin du Soleil is a certified organic lavender farm, cradled in the rainshadow of Washington State’s Olympic Mountains. The farm is located on the Olympic Peninsula four miles north of “sunny” Sequim, Washington. Surrounded by hundreds of acres of protected wildlife, the farm was planted in 1999 on land that was part of a dairy farm established in the 1880’s. Victorian gardens, ponds, fruit trees and lavender fields encompass the landscape with the Strait of Juan de Fuca beyond. Thousands of lavender plants on 10+ acres create a wonderfully fragrant vista at the farm. State-of-the-art lavender oil distillation provides the quality certified organic lavender essential oil used to produce unique and beautiful lavender products for the bath and body, the home and the garden: lavender candles, lavender sachets,bulk dried lavender and lavender soap. Jardin du Soleil lavender farm invites you to an experience that will delight the senses! The farm and gardens are open daily throughout the summer; the plants are in bloom from the end of June through August, with harvesting starting in July. Pick your own lavender bouquets or take home some of these aromatic plants. Our farm’s retail store and website offer those distinctive lavender products and gifts that enhance your life and home. And don’t forget to mark your calendar for the Annual Lavender Festival the 3rd weekend in July, or any of our special events held at the farm. Paul and Jordan Schiefen invite you to experience lavender at Jardin du Soleil. Enjoy our lavender farm’s fields and gardens, and partake in the pastoral beauty of the Olympic Peninsula, while soothing your soul and stimulating your senses. The magic of Jardin du Soleil will ensure that your visit is one that you will look forward to repeating. .

notes: We are an educational farm located in the tiny village of Venersborg, just east of Battle Ground, WA. We offer classes and overnight farmstays so you can immerse yourself in the rhythm of our peaceful organic farm. Have you ever heard the air shimmer with the sound of a cow lowing to her young calf? Wonderful sound. Our biodynamic farm is Certified Naturally Grown, a grass roots alternative to USDA certification. We teach classes about compassionate care for bees, backyard chickens for urban folks, biodynamic compost-making, cooking and preserving food, a career course in horse bodywork and lots of other topics. Each fall we host an apple tasting at our local one-room schoolhouse with over 200 kinds of heirloom apples.Our farm is home to grass fed cows (simmenthal, jersey, swiss), chickens, seasonal heirloom turkeys and bees from wild swarms. We have orchards, grape arbors, a small greenhouse, and flower, berry, herb and vegetable gardens. On our website you can sign up for our newsletter that tells upcoming events on the farm, when new baby animals are born and anything else that’s going on. We also offer a lot of educational classes about honeybees, chickens, biodynamic compost, compost tea, and kitchen crafts. We also do agritourism and have people come and stay on the farm and learn what we do by participating.

products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Eggs; Eggs (Chicken); Fruit & Berries; Apples; Blackberries; Raspberries; Meat & Poultry; Chicken; Livestock for Sale; Pork; Vegetables & Herbs; Asian Greens/Bok Choy; Asparagus; Basil; Beans (Green/Yellow); Beets; Bell peppers; Cabbage; Carrots; Chard; Chives; Corn; Cucumbers; Dill; Herbs & Botanicals; Herbs (Fresh); Kale; Kohlrabi; Lemongrass; Onions; Potatoes; Pumpkins; Root Vegetables; Squash (Summer); Squash (Winter); Tomatoes (Heirloom); Locally Made; Local Food Box; Reusable Waste
notes: We are a small family farm surrounded by forests of evergreen trees in Bellingham, Washington. We are close enough to the city but far enough away from mono-culture farming to assure that our chickens are never exposed to herbicides and pesticides used with industrialized agriculture. Our chickens love the fresh air, forests, rich organic pasture cover crops and the best care we can provide. For this holiday season, we are offering farm theme greeting cards that were designed at the farm featuring our very own farm animals. The cards were locally printed by a small professional print shop. Every card purchased helps in our farm’s heritage chicken and Kunekune pig preservation efforts, to keep the birds & pigs that we love for many more generations to come. We are focused on the breeds that we raise. The chicks come from breeding stock that has been selected from large preservation flocks of birds. Our goal is to provide our customers with unique as well as hardy breeds of poultry and an opportunity to raise pastoral rare breeds of chicken that will thrive and be an asset to your farm and fun entertainment for your family. Watching our chicks grow into adult birds enables us to select the best ones for our breeding programs and gives us the unique opportunity to produce some of the best tasting heritage chickens in North America. We are a leader in our marketplace in offering fruit or veggie finished pasture-raised birds. We sell chickens for the table finished with in-season produce carefully grown on our farms whether it’s pumpkin, apple, wild blackberries and more. We added KuneKune pigs (pronounced “cooney cooney”) to the farm just a couple of years ago. We have been loving every minute of it! I’m sure you are thinking, why not add bacon, but that’s not why we did it. These pigs are wonderful grazers with minimal impact to our forest and land. No more allergies from mowing and when in proper rotation, no more weed eating the fence lines. They are our almost carbon neutral, non-petrol fueled landscapers! With the added bonus of being delicious too. We offer piglets in the fall and they are a delight to have on any small farm other than the occasional escapee. But when they do escape, a few apples or watermelon will have them running right back home. Our KuneKune pigs are unvaccinated and are raised with a great life on pasture year-round. We practice biosecurity to provide our customers with healthy and happy birds. We do not have visitors to the farm. Unfortunately, shoes and vehicle tires are a pathway for contamination. Our farm is tested bi-annually with the National Poultry Improvement Program. Pastured artisan chicken and pastured Kunekune pork free delivery in Bellingham within 5 miles of Bellingham International Airport. Pasture-raised chicken delivery to Seattle, Everett, Lynnwood, Ballard, and beyond for a small fee once a week. We can ship to you within Washington State, one day delivery.

notes: The Common Acre begins with the soil. Our mission is to restore relationships between people and the land through ecology, agriculture, and art. We reconnect humans with nature through the medium of food and seek to restore a living food system that feeds our minds and nourishes our communities. Our collaborative programs transform marginalized land into biodiverse pollinator habitat and community farms, which in turn create space for inspirational cultural convenings. We also partner with scientists to improve our understanding of native pollinator ecosystems and feed that research back into our restoration work. We believe urban food systems are key to creating healthy communities. Food is more than what we eat: it’s a medium through which we can connect, both mentally and physically, to our neighbors and our surroundings. Our health comes from the soil, and the pollinators that complete the growing process. We bring people closer to their food and each other through a network of community farms and wild bee habitat projects. You can visit each of our four community farms in Seattle during their weekly open hours to learn about organic farming, lend a hand, harvest, or just meet your neighbors! We donate 100% of produce to local residents and a network of seven partner meal programs and food banks.

Our daughter and her family live nearby and help with taste-testing and quality control. Many years ago, we realized that if our farm was to survive we would have to have much more control over growing, harvesting, and selling than we could get by working through a traditional packing warehouse. We began packing and selling our own fruit, and have been fortunate to work with several great local NW retailers directly. Our orchard is quite small by industry standards, so we have to pay close attention to quality as well as quantity of what we grow. name: Okanogan Highlands Lavender Farm
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Flowers, Nursery & Trees; Lavender; Vegetables & Herbs; Herbs & Botanicals; Herbs (Fresh)
notes: Okanogan Highlands Lavender Farm is a non profit, eco-education farm in rural North Central Washington. Our off grid, mountain top farm uses solar and wind energy to run the farm house and processing building where we make high quality wellness products using our lavender and other quality organic ingredients. The ultimate goal of Okanogan Highlands Lavender Farm is to highlight sustainability as a farm in the shrub steppe region of North Central Washington State. We consider the natural environment in all that we do at OHLF. We grow lavender organically and naturally, and though we do not currently have USDA certification, we are confident in our knowledge that we are doing our best to maintain the delicate symbiotic balance of the soil. Through the use of wind and solar energy, we’ve drastically reduced our use of fossil fuels. We trade fairly in the local market, offering a variety of lavender products both online and local retail, but the true value of the farm is in its capacity to support environmental education and foster contemplation of this beautiful ecosystem in which we live. Regarding where to find our products other than online – we have, in the past, sold at farmers markets (and may, in the future sell at farmers markets again) but currently we are selling at small retailers like Paws Produce Market (Oroville) and nurseries like Baker’s Acres in Tonasket and ‘Chelle’s in Okanogan. Caso’s Country Foods is a new retail store in Okanogan, carries our wellness products and our new lavender hydrosol all purpose cleaner. We aim to make OHLF a beacon of possibility for people looking for a more sustainable, more deeply connected existence. By purchasing our lavender products you help the organization establish educational outlets for people interested in environmental stewardship and sustainable living.

notes: Mountainview Blueberry Farm is a large U-Pick blueberry farm located in the beautiful farming community of Snohomish in the Snohomish River Valley. The farm is nestled down low against a hillside, overlooking surrounding farms framed by the Cascade Mountain Range. On a clear day, you can even see Mount Baker to the north. The farm boasts nine acres of luscious blueberries featuring several different varieties. Many of the varieties herald from days gone by and are not to be found anymore. All these different varieties provide you with several unique flavors and sizes. Originally established by the Uran family in the 1940s, the blueberry farm provided for the founders until its sale in 1976 to the Phillips family. The Phillips established a new home on the farm in 1979 where they raised their family until selling to the Simpson family in 1996. The Simpsons also raised their family on the farm and took wonderful care of it until they sold it in 2007. In 2007 the farm was purchased by Keith and Janet Stocker, fourth generation farmers in the Snohomish River Valley. We, Keith and Janet along with our sons Ivan and Raleigh Stocker, were thrilled to be able to purchase the farm from our friends the Simpsons a few years ago. We are happy to be the new stewards of this beautiful farm and piece of history. Please come out and see why.

notes: Moua Farm has been in business since 1994 that started off selling only produce at the farmer’s market. Chao’s parents immigrated from Thailand to the U.S. in 1987. Both were born in the highlands of Laos where they met each other. Chao and Mao is among a generation of the Hmong living in Southeast Asia. They would share stories to their children about life growing up in poverty, and the only way to survive is farming. Every morning, they would tend to their parents’ acres of land where they grew vegetables to sell at the street market. Their agricultural skills was carried over here in the U.S. to start their own business in Seattle, WA. When selling flowers became a booming business, Chao and Mao made the decision to cultivate, plant, and grow seasonal flowers to sell in the mid 1990’s. notes: Island Fresh farm is located on beautiful Marrowstone Island, a serene, protected spot in the rain shadow between Kilisut Harbor and Admiralty Inlet. We believe in sustainability and farm to restore the land through its use. We are not certified organic but grow our crops without use of harmful pesticides or herbicides and use only natural fertilizers to amend the soil. Our pigs are content as they rotate through grassy pastures, tilling the land and fertilizing as they go. Their diet is balanced with locally sourced grains, fodder (sprouted seeds), local whey, eggs, and windfall fruit. The chickens, ducks, and turkeys free range to control flies, slugs, and other buggy pests while contributing their own fertilizer. Our flock of sheep rotates through pastures to keep the fence lines mowed and our Kiko goats clear the brush. Happy healthy animals are more delicious and more nutritious. We use New Zealand designed fencing in combination with guardian animals to keep predators wild and our family of domestic food animals safely protected. We raise our animals humanely so we (and you) can eat delicious healthful food without guilt.

notes: We are 8 acres of vegetables, fruit and herbs, powered by a few horses and some humans. We are a values-driven farm. We believe in fighting for and standing up for other people, other species and our planet. We know climate change is real. We celebrate diversity. We work to pay our employees a fair, living wage for reasonable hours of work. We believe feeding people is activism, and we recognize that in order to make a living and pay our crew fairly, our produce is not necessarily affordable for all. We donate some produce to the regional food bank distribution center and are looking for other ways to increase accessibility. We understand that this work is a journey, not a destination, and we welcome feedback. We also recognize that our farm exists on the stolen lands of the Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla, Cayuse and Walla Walla. We are seeking ways to turn these words into meaningful action. We aim to grow high quality, nutrient dense, colorfully diverse produce, available year round. We seed a mix of open pollinated and hybrid varieties, selected for both the best eating quality and exceptional performance in the field. We grow produce that we want to eat, and hope you enjoy it too. notes: Good Rain Farm is located in Camas, WA – 22 miles from downtown Portland. Food sovereignty, honorable earth stewardship and community empowerment are our guiding principles. We have one acre of vegetable and fruit crops with an emphasis on native edibles while also raising heritage breed meat rabbits. We also have a second site at the EMCSWCD Headwaters Farm Incubator in Gresham, Oregon. Good Rain translates to x̌ast sq̓it (hast squeit) in the traditional language of the Sinixt or Arrow Lakes Peoples. Farm Founder Michelle is of Sinixt ancestry. At x̌ast sq̓it Farm we explore our relationship with this land, we decolonize and question our notions of ‘food’ and ‘nourishment’. We support our community to these ends. Providing a variety of produce with an emphasis on first foods, the farm centers conversations around food sovereignty. Through our internship and food offerings we are building a stronger connection to place through positive hands-on learning around food justice, sustainable land stewardship, farming practices and local ethnobotany. The Good Rain Farm CSA is primarily vegetables, herbs, fruits, and edible flowers and a limited amount of native edibles included. A standard share includes 8-12 different fresh items. People’s eating habits are very different, but a standard share may provide enough vegetables for two veggie-loving adults or a family of four omnivores.

products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Eggs; Eggs (Chicken); Fruit & Berries; Apples; Pears; Strawberries; Vegetables & Herbs; Basil; Beans (Green/Yellow); Chives; Collard Greens; Cucumbers; Dill; Herbs & Botanicals; Herbs (Fresh); Root Vegetables; Tomatoes; Tomatoes (Cherry); Locally Made; Yarn, Fiber & Wool
notes: Located on the stunning Key Peninsula, Foxglove Farm is a small, family-owned farm specializing in fruits and vegetables and locally grown and produced yarn and fiber. Focusing on heirloom and unusual produce varieties such as Strawberry apples and Tatsoi greens, we implement organic growing practices and strive for a closed system farming environment by purposely selecting additions that serve multiple functionalities benefiting our bio-network. Our farm family includes seven Pygora goats, two Nigerian Dwarf goats, Shetland and Salish sheep who are well-loved and an integral part of our closed system process. With our livestock, we create small-batch, single-source yarn and fiber, control invasive species such as Himalayan blackberry, enrich our compost, and maintain an intensely managed pasture. We work closely with Pierce Conservation District to protect our waterways and to restore the small stream on our property back to a salmon-spawning site. Our values drive us to invest in our local economy and support and promote other Washington farmers, especially women and people of color.

notes: Courage to Grow Farms is a family-owned, first-generation regenerative farm located on 30 acres in the heart of the Palouse. We currently steward the land with about 5.5 acres in active production, where we grow over 60 varieties of vegetables and herbs, along with melons, berries, and other seasonal fruits. Our farm is managed using regenerative practices that prioritize soil health and eliminate synthetic fertilizers, herbicides, and pesticides. In addition to what we grow ourselves, we partner with carefully vetted local regenerative farms that raise grass-fed beef, pasture-raised pork, and additional fruit, ensuring the same land-stewarding principles are followed. Together, we offer a diverse range of truly local, responsibly raised food. Through our CSA and farm delivery program, we deliver directly to households across Whitman, Lincoln, Spokane, Stevens, and Kootenai counties, helping make fresh, regenerative food accessible while strengthening the regional food system. Looking toward the future, we plan to transition much of our remaining acreage into a silvopasture system—integrating trees, pasture, and livestock into a resilient ecosystem. This system will include fruit and nut trees, berry hedgerows, and rotational grazing for cattle, pigs, and poultry. The trees and shrubs will provide shade for animals and act as natural pasture dividers, while livestock contribute fertility through manure, creating a symbiotic relationship that builds soil health and supports a thriving, sustainable farm ecosystem. At Courage to Grow Farms, our mission is simple: grow nourishing food, steward the land responsibly, and build a resilient local food network that feeds our communities. 🌱

notes: The Broken Shovel Kiwi Farm was started in 2011 on a 1/2 acre lot in Burien, with 59 hardy kiwi vines (involving seven different varieties). The Mossyrock location was added in 2016, with 140 younger vines now growing there (making for a total of 199 hardy kiwi vines, and nine different varieties on the two properties). The incentive for starting this farm was the discovery that various studies have determined that kiwis are “the most nutrient dense of all the most commonly consumed fruits” in the world. This was followed by the discovery that there were only a handful of small farms in the United States growing hardy kiwis, and fresh hardy kiwis were, for all practical purposes, almost impossible to find in the State of Washington. So, as they say, one thing led to another, and while there are an increasing number of growers of hardy kiwis in Washington and Oregon, Broken Shovel Kiwi Farm continues to be unique in picking and selling their different hardy kiwi varieties only after they’ve ripened and reached their full level of sweetness and taste. notes: THE COCKTAIL FARM: The Simple Goodness Cocktail Farm is, as far as we can tell, the world’s first exclusive cocktail farm. Here we grow a variety of herbs, edible flowers, fruits, and vegetables with one goal in mind: make delicious drinks. Located on 10 acres in Buckley, WA, the farm was purchased in the Spring of 2013 by Venise and Ross Cunningham. The garden acres are devoted to growing for Simple Goodness Sisters, including Simple Goodness Syrups, the Cocktail Farm Club membership boxes, and the Simple Goodness Soda Shop menu. SIMPLE GOODNESS SYRUPS: SIMPLE SYRUPS, BETTER DRINKS Organic cane sugar and whole ingredient based, sourced from family farms Farmed in the Pacific Northwest, Simple Goodness Sisters syrups capture the intense, pure flavors of a season and naturally preserve them. We grow the majority of the ingredients for the syrups on our family farm in Buckley, WA, and source whatever we can’t grow with intention, supporting others using ethical growing practices. The syrups are made from scratch in small batches in Washington state using recyclable packaging. COCKTAIL FARM CLUB: A CSA FOR COCKTAILS DELIVERED TO YOUR DOOR Enliven your drink routine by bringing the Simple Goodness Cocktail Farm to your glass! Imagine you’re taking a tour through a bountiful garden, stepping between rows bursting with sweet, savory, floral and herbaceous plants, when you’re handed a fragrant cocktail, freshly mixed from those same ingredients. Now imagine having that drink experience from the comfort of your home, guided by sisters Venise, a farmer, and Belinda, a bartender, who grow all natural, preservative-free drink mixers on their 10 acre cocktail farm. With every Cocktail Farm Club release, you’ll experience the best of each season’s harvest through micro-batches of our garden to glass mixers and garnishes. You’ll also be supporting our family farm at the foothills of Mount Rainier, WA, where we farm using regenerative agriculture practices. The Cocktail Farm Club is our farm’s version of a traditional farm share CSA or like a cocktail mixer “wine club.” Each release allows for a variety of drink variations, and will include recipes and drink education so you can become a garden to glass mixologist at home. WANT TO VISIT US? COME TO OUR OFF FARM AGRITOURISM CENTER, THE SIMPLE GOODNESS SODA SHOP: Our home away from home, the Simple Goodness Soda Shop is a tasting room, a farm to table cafe, and our production headquarters. Just a few miles from our farm, the Soda Shop is the family friendly bar of our dreams. Inhabiting one of the few original historic buildings in Wilkeson, the earliest incorporated town in the state of Washington, the Soda Shop continues the building’s 120+ year tradition of serving good people good food and drinks. Come to shop and sample our products in person, and stay for happy hour or dinner! Here, we take soda fountain classics and craft cocktails and give them a modern day twist, with garden to glass flavors. The casual fare is seasonal, homey, and often doused in syrup. Rhubarb Vanilla Bean margaritas share a menu with Apple Pie Lattes, Marionberry Mint sundaes, and hot, melty sandwiches. Bring your families to enjoy our open seating, big outdoor dining yard with games (dog friendly), friendly atmosphere and warm hospitality.

name: Left Foot Farm
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Dairy; Milk (Cow); Eggs; Eggs (Chicken); Locally Made; Dairy Products
notes: Left Foot Farm is a 5-acre family farm near Mount Rainier in Washington, currently raising about 100 dairy goats. We are a licensed Grade A Raw Milk dairy, and proud to share great tasting milk from our girls.There are so many variables that go into milk production and we are always learning. Pasture rotation, types of forage, varieties of grain and fodder—these are some of the elements we are either experimenting with now, or plan to examine more closely soon.Left Foot seeks to utilize the most sustainable and organic methods possible in a dairy. We breed our goats year-round on a rotating basis, with the goal of producing conformational and productive dairy goats in a caring and humane setting. The Farm tests annually for CAE, CL, Brucellosis, TB, and Q Fever.We are grateful to have a healthy, happy herd. Our crew is blessed to enjoy life on the farm with the goats. Please schedule a visit with us and check out Left Foot Farm! Thank you for your interest in our herd. We raise Nigerian Dwarf goats who spend their days roaming the green pastures in the foothills of Mt. Rainier.Our goats are fed a nutritious diet and milked with care to produce high-quality raw milk, rich in vitamins and nutrients.Why Raw Milk?Raw milk is just as it comes from the goat. It is filtered and cooled, but otherwise unprocessed. “Raw” means that it has not been pasteurized, a process by which the milk is heated to a high temperature to kill harmful bacteria. Pasteurization also kills vitamins A, C, B-complex, and 20% of the iodine in raw milk.Locally Made, In Small BatchesThese days, many people want to limit their exposure to mass-produced, overly-processed foods. Our milk is made the old-fashioned way: small batches from your local farm!Is Raw Milk Safe?Even though raw milk is not pasteurized, it must still meet federal food safety standards set by the FDA and the U.S. Public Health Service.You should only buy raw milk from a farm with strict health and sanitation practices. We are a certified Grade “A” Raw Milk Producer, and our facility has been inspected and licensed as a Milk Processing Plant by the Washington State Department of Agriculture.While raw milk poses a little health risk to most people, those with weakened immune systems, such as pregnant women, very young children, and the elderly, should not consume raw milk.Store your milk at 40° F. Shelf life is about two weeks

notes: We are growing flowers organically at Historic Faraway, our farm situated on Filucy Bay on the Key Peninsula. We are not open to the public at this time but when our barn restoration is complete we will host classes & workshops. For now we do pop-ups to sell fresh flowers and also fill special orders. Faraway Flower Farm is located on Filucy Bay, in a town called Longbranch, on the Key Peninsula. We are about 40 minutes from Tacoma, Washington. Faraway Flower Farm is part of the original Far-A-Way, a historic waterfront estate founded in 1914. We are currently restoring the buildings and landscaping to its former glory, although in many ways it will be much better than it's ever been! At Faraway Flower Farm we are using organic methods to grow stunning flowers and fragrant foliage for the floral industry, and for anyone who wants more fresh flowers in their life!We are currently not open to the public, but once our 100 year old barn restoration is complete we will have cut flowers, foliage, herbs, and interesting plants available for sale at special pop-up events as well as floral arrangements, seeds, tubers and seedlings, depending on the time of year. In my Etsy shop I have sold hundreds of dahlia tubers and thousands of easy-to-grow seeds over the past couple of years. I can't wait to have a retail shop to offer these things easily to our local flower friends. We will also sell items with a "sense of place"; items that showcase the bounty of this amazing area, such as aromatic wreathes, hand-harvested sea salts, and other handcrafted delights. Besides the retail shop the barn restoration includes a kitchen with a classroom, a floral design shop within the retail store, and the 1000 sq foot loft is an open workspace that features French doors on all 4 sides where you can take in the breath-taking views of Filucy Bay, the Upper Flower Field, our menagerie of animals including miniature horses and the other historic buildings we are in the process of restoring with meticulous attention to detail. At the same time we making major improvements to the landscaping and hardscaping, spread over about 4 of the 7 acres. High on my priority list is creating a variety of perennial beds that will not only make the estate more beautiful but will add to the offerings for floral designers and those who love to buy cut flowers for their homes.Please follow our social media which includes not only Faraway Flower Farm but Historic Faraway as well, to be kept up-to-date on our progress. I also have a website and Facebook page called Learn To Preserve, where I share helpful advice and inspiration as a Master Food Preserver. Thanks so much for your interest, Brook Hurst Stephens

Then, Nelida moved to Washington, where she learned organic practices and gained experience growing 100% organic products that you can enjoy with total confidence. Pure Nelida produce is grown with the utmost honesty, effort, and skill unique to Nelida. Nelida’s personal interest in organic products comes from her son’s diagnosis of leukemia and her suspicion that the disease arose due to the many years the family spent working among the pesticide-ridden fields of California. After a long battle, Nelida ultimately lost her son to this disease. ​Pure Nelida Organic Produce is an independent business that uses agricultural practices that are free of pesticides. Its products are fresh and certified organic from the state of Washington, and come directly from the fields of Skagit county to your table, ready to be fully enjoyed for their nutricious, fresh, and Pure Nelida flavor. Ella y sus familia trabajaron y vivieron bajo los rayos del sol y los pesticidas. Ahora después de todas estas experiencias acumuladas , Nelida aprendió a cultivar y experimentar con productos orgánicos elaborando productos que usted puede saborear y disfrutar con la confianza y seguridad de que son 100 por ciento productos orgánicos elaborados con el esfuerzo, honradez y experiencia que solo “Pure Nelida Organic Produce” le da a sus productos. El interés personal de Nélida por los productos orgánicos se debe principalmente a la batalla contra la leucemia que su familia ha tenido en los últimos años y también por la sospecha de que ella y su familia siempre trabajaron en los campos de California bajo las pesticidas—terminando con la pérdida de su hijo por cancer. name: Mama Bird Farm
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Flowers, Nursery & Trees; Cut Flowers; Vegetables & Herbs; Artichokes; Arugula; Asparagus; Basil; Beans (Green/Yellow); Beets; Braising Mix; Broccoli; Brussels Sprouts; Cabbage; Carrots; Cauliflower; Celery; Chard; Cilantro; Corn; Cucumbers; Dill; Eggplant; Garlic; Kale; Lettuce; Mustard Greens; Onions; Peas; Peppers (Hot); Peppers (Sweet); Potatoes; Pumpkins; Radishes; Salad Greens; Spinach; Squash (Summer); Squash (Winter); Tomatoes; Tomatoes (Cherry)
notes: Mama Bird is a 6 acre produce farm started by Lars Johnson and Mara Lawrence in 2014, second generation farmers drawn toward this work in the hopes to grow healthy local food for our community and family, and to steer away from the industrial food system. We specialize in a unique baby greens mix, heirloom tomatoes, and a variety of veggies, cut flowers, arrangements for weddings and seed crops. You can find our produce and flowers at local restaurants and grocery stores as well as the Puget Sound Food Hub that has broadened our reach to Skagit, Whatcom and King counties. We love our wild birds, salamanders, bugs and natural ecosystem, so we don’t use any synthetic pesticides, herbicides or fungicides, Ever! We rotate and grow cover crops to enrich and add nutrients to our soil. Our little farm is surrounded by a creek, lots of trees and therefore has a healthy interwoven relationship of farm and forest. Mama Bird started out as raw land, an open field for grazing sheep. Over the years we have slowly built roads, a processing facility, greenhouses, brought in power, drilled a well, along with growing produce and flowers for our community. We grow fresh food that tastes alive and fills you with goodness! Thanks for checking us out and supporting small local farms!

name: Oak Meadows Farm
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Dairy; Milk (Cow); Eggs; Eggs (Chicken); Eggs (Other); Farm Supplies; Animal Feed; Compost; Fruit & Berries; Apples; Berries; Grapes; Pears; Strawberries; Meat & Poultry; Bacon; Beef; Chicken; Ground Meat; Ham; Lamb; Livestock for Sale; Pork; Poultry; Sausage; Turkey; Grains & Pulses; Wheat; Seafood; Salmon
notes: Oak Meadows Farm is a family-owned, pasture-based poultry and livestock farm located just north of Bellingham, WA. What began as a small farm specializing in pasture-raised chicken and pork has grown into a regional hub for local food through our expanded on-farm store, Acorn Market at Oak Meadows. At Acorn Market, we bring together the best of our own pasture-raised products and an ever-growing selection from other local farms and artisans — including grass-fed beef, lamb, and yak, small-batch cheeses, honey, kombucha, baked goods, and seasonal produce. Our goal is to make it easier for our community to eat local year-round by offering a curated selection of high-quality, regionally produced foods under one roof. Our pasture-raised chickens are moved onto fresh pasture at 3–4 weeks old, where they forage freely on diverse grasses and insects while enjoying Non-GMO, corn- and soy-free feed made from locally grown wheat, peas, and alfalfa. Our pigs are also raised on open pasture, and our partner farms’ beef and lamb are 100% grass-fed and grass-finished. Hormones, steroids, and antibiotics are never used in any of our livestock production. In addition to meats and eggs, we also operate Oak Meadows Hatchery, where we breed and hatch our own lines of specialty broiler chickens and Coturnix quail. Broiler chicks, quail eggs, and hatching eggs are available seasonally for other farms and backyard producers. Whether you visit Acorn Market at Oak Meadows for locally raised meats, farm-fresh eggs, or to discover new foods from regional producers, you’ll find a place where transparency, collaboration, and true local flavor come together.

notes: Since 2011, we have been learning to nurture crops in our unique micro-climates of our warm southern exposed hillsides & the cooler lowland fields. notes: City Sprouts Farm builds community resilience by stewarding a productive urban farm space where people can come together to learn, increase food access, and demonstrate how community vitality can grow through our food system. We are a one-acre urban farm located in the Birchwood Neighborhood of Bellingham. The goals of our farm are to increase food access, practice ecological and regenerative growing methods, and to bring people together to learn and find belonging within our community and ecosystem. Our programming is embedded within Western Washington University’s Center for Community Learning and we provide multiple entry points for students to engage in local agriculture. We host WWU students through seasonal employment, classes, work parties, internships, and independent studies and more. City Sprouts Farm is located on the ancestral homelands of the Lummi Nation, Nooksack Tribe and other federally recognized and unrecognized tribes. We are visitors here and are indebted to the generations of people who have stewarded the land and waterways of this region since time immemorial.

products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Eggs; Eggs (Chicken); Fruit & Berries; Blackberries; Blueberries; Raspberries; Strawberries; Vegetables & Herbs; Artichokes; Arugula; Asian Greens/Bok Choy; Basil; Beans (Green/Yellow); Beets; Bell peppers; Braising Mix; Broccoli; Broccolini; Brussels Sprouts; Cabbage; Carrots; Cauliflower; Celeriac; Celery; Chard; Chicories; Chives; Cilantro; Collard Greens; Corn; Cucumbers; Daikon; Dill; Eggplant; Endive; Escarole; Fennel; Garlic; Garlic Greens; Garlic Scapes; Green Onions; Herbs (Fresh); Kale; Kohlrabi; Leeks; Lemongrass; Lettuce; Mustard Greens; Onions; Parsley; Parsnips; Pea Vines; Peas; Peppers (Hot); Peppers (Sweet); Potatoes; Potatoes (Sweet); Pumpkins; Radicchio; Radishes; Root Vegetables; Salad Greens; Shallots; Sorrel; Spinach; Squash (Summer); Squash (Winter); Thyme; Tomatillos; Tomatoes; Tomatoes (Cherry); Tomatoes (Heirloom); Turnips; Wild Greens
notes: A fifth Generation Skagitonian, I grew up on my family’s farm/homestead. Feeding the horses, cows, goats and pigs were just normal everyday chores; so was helping Nana with the daily, seasonal tasks of the garden. ‘Garden’ would not really be the scale appropriate term to describe her half acre of hand cultivated passion that we ate out of year-round; but the space will always be Nana’s Garden. She grew food regeneratively and organically in the old ways; modern fertilizers, organic or not, never entered the soil. We were continuously making compost using the farms’ animal manure and bedding and would apply it to the garden every fall after summer crops were done. Nana’s Garden still has the best soil on the farm. Foothills Farm is modeled after these same core values. We are stewards of our soil; we have a responsibility to our land, our community and our employees to care for and leave this land better than we received it. Every decision regarding the farm is made through this lens. Currently, Foothills stewards ~200 acres in Eastern Skagit County. Most of the year we will have 100-120 acres in some form of legume-based cover crop with cows or poultry mob grazing; doubling the functions of adding fertility. There are several acres of berries; currently mostly strawberries. We grow annual row-crops for all 4 seasons and at the height of the summer planting season may have close to 100 acres of 90+ varieties of vegetables. We operate at several farmers markets a week in the summer and three year-round markets. We also wholesale to a diverse mix of restaurants, grocery stores, food banks (including Helping Hands in SW), school districts (Concrete and SW), CSA aggregators and we run our own CSA as well. We have taken this core ethos of regenerative stewardship with us into how we operate both in business and in life. If there is an opportunity to help and give back knowledge that we have gained, we will take it. We are a species that thrives in co-operation, and we will only begin to be able to obtain our full potential through co-operation with each other.

name: Nerka Sea Frozen Salmon
products_text: Locally Raised, Harvested, Grown; Seafood; Salmon
notes: Nerka Sea Frozen Salmon has supplied Whatcom restaurants & retailers with premium quality wild Alaskan salmon since 2002. Our kings & coho are hook & line caught, thanked, pressure-bled, cleaned & processed, blast-frozen at -38 degrees & glazed. Ours is a sea-to-plate story, & we tell it with love.

notes: Butterflies migrate long distances over several generations, guided by nature. We migrated from Mexico 9 years ago to work on organic farms in Washington and now we have our own family farm! We are a 9.5 acre farm located in Everson that grows around 60 varieties of vegetables. Mariposa Farm works hard to offer high quality fresh vegetables. Our farm offers fresh picked vegetables, herbs, and berries. We grow a wide variety of produce and we can be found at Bellingham and Seattle farmers markets. Our goal is to provide fresh local produce to our community.
